As President Donald Trump signed an executive order upending the federal guidance for childhood vaccines, social media was more focused on a woman standing behind him during the announcement repeatedly nodding her head.

On Monday, Trump signed an executive order calling for revamped childhood vaccine recommendations that promote his long-held — and also discredited — theory that childhood shots should be spaced out over several appointments.

However, many social media users were far more interested with Jayme Franklin, the CEO of the conservative media and lifestyle brand The Conservateur and former Trump staffer.

Footage circulating on social media showed a smiling Franklin alongside Trump and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in the Oval Office as the president announced the changes for federal childhood vaccinations.

Franklin could be seen holding her hand over her stomach while repeatedly nodding her head in agreement— actions that seemed to leave some Internet users perplexed, while others opted to nickname her “bobble head.”

open image in gallery The Internet was intrigued by Jayme Franklin’s appearance during President Donald Trump’s announcement on childhood vaccines on Monday ( Getty )

“It’s a three ring circus between bobble head bimbo, babbling Bobby and Sleepy Don!” one X user exclaimed while sharing a clip of the announcement.

“Who is this young woman holding her belly as Trump is sleeping and why is she there?” another X user questioned.

Another curious social media user chimed in, asking, “What in the cyborg MAGA fembot shit is going on here?”

“Forget Trump....What is up with the woman holding her stomach???” another commentator added.

Franklin has not publicly acknowledged social media’s response to her appearance, but did write on X that she was “honored” to join the president in the Oval Office for the signing of the executive order.

In a statement to The Independent, she elaborated, “I was honored to join President Trump for the historic Executive Order signing focused on giving parents greater freedom to consult with their pediatricians and make the decisions they believe are best for their children.”

open image in gallery It was not immediately clear what role Franklin had in the executive order ( AP )

When asked what role Franklin had in the executive order, White House spokesman Kush Desai told The Independent, “Jayme Franklin represents the countless parents whose questions and concerns about America’s childhood vaccine schedule have been either ignored or mocked. President Trump promised to realign America’s vaccine schedule to match those of our peer nations, and his executive order yesterday reflects how the Administration is delivering with Gold Standard Science.”

Franklin started The Conservateur, a media and lifestyle brand for young conservative Christian women in November 2019.

Before starting her brand, she worked in Republican politics and conservative media, according to her Aspen Ideas profile.

She previously worked as an associate editor and administrative and production assistant for Fox News, where she now appears as a guest commentator.

Before working in conservative media, she was director of correspondence during the first Trump administration, and also worked as a coalitions coordinator for Trump’s 2020 campaign.

The man who tried to assassinate Ronald Reagan in an attempt to impress Jodie Foster has wished the movie star well in a new interview.

John Hinckley Jr., 71, spoke about the two-time Oscar winner with the Mark Joseph Show, according to Entertainment Weekly’s preview of the interview before its release Wednesday.

“I just wish Jodie Foster well, you know,” Hinckley said, per the publication. “I don’t really see her movies, but I wish her well, and I know she’s doing quite well. And that’s all I can say is just, I wish Jodie well, and I hope she has a good life.”

Hinckley infamously shot President Ronald Reagan outside of the Hilton Hotel in Washington, D.C., on March 30, 1981. Reagan was wounded in the attack, along with three other people: Press Secretary James Brady, police officer Thomas Delahanty and Secret Service agent Timothy McCarthy.

Shortly after the shooting, it came to light that Hinckley — who was 25 at the time — had carried out the assassination attempt to get Foster’s attention after spending months calling her and sending her love letters.

open image in gallery John Hinckley Jr. said he wishes Jodie Foster the best after previously stalking her ( CBS/Getty )

He had become obsessed with the actor, who was 18 at the time, after seeing her 1976 movie Taxi Driver, in which she plays a child prostitute alongside Robert De Niro’s character Travis Bickle, who attempts to kill a politician.

Hinckley told the Mark Joseph Show: “I wanted to have a union with Jodie Foster and live the rest of my life with her and all these things that, of course, were delusional. But I was believing those things at the time, so the best outcome would have been a union with Jodie Foster.”

The Independent has contacted Foster’s representatives for further comment.

open image in gallery John Hinckley Jr. was tackled to the ground after shooting President Ronald Reagan in Washington, DC, in March 1981 ( AFP/Getty )

After a seven-week long trial in 1982, Hinckley was found not guilty by reason of insanity for the attempted assassination. He went on to spend 35 years in a psychiatric facility before being released in 2022.

Since his release, Hinckley has openly spoken about his remorse for his actions and is pursuing a career as a singer-songwriter.

Foster has not spoken about the experience except for what she said was the first and last time in a 1982 article for Esquire titled “Why Me?” and published months after the verdict.

“John Hinckley's greatest crime was the confusion of love and obsession,” she wrote. “The trivialization of love is something I will never forgive him. Love is blissful. Obsession is pitiful, self indulgent.”

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register or login to an existing telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football launched on August 10, 2026. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.

How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games. Last season Mark Flekken came out on top with 153 saves for Brentford, so it will be interesting to see how Caoimhin Kelleher gets on this season.



What counts as a Save?



A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

Sports.title: SunRisers beat Super Giants to reach Hundred eliminator
Sports.content:
Reigning champions SunRisers Leeds snatched a spot in the women's Hundred eliminator by beating Manchester Super Giants by 41 runs in a winner-takes-all game at Old Trafford.

In a shoot-out for the final place in the top three, Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off 36 balls helped Leeds leapfrog their opponents and set up an eliminator clash against Southern Brave.

The Australian all-rounder hit nine boundaries, including three sixes, as the visitors posted 166-4 after being put in to bat.

Visiting spinner Jess Jonassen took 3-21, while Deepti Sharma and Sutherland claimed two wickets apiece, as Manchester were restricted to 125-8 in reply and exited the competition after slipping to fourth place in the standings.

Second-placed Leeds will continue their title defence against Southern Brave on Friday at The Oval, with table-topping Trent Rockets awaiting the winner in Sunday's final at Lord's.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player UNBELIEVABLE athletic fielding from SunRisers' Phoebe Litchfield to prevent a six

Sutherland, the Match Hero, said: "It's the beauty of being an all-rounder, you're in the game all the time, and I love competing, especially in a match we were calling a final. We had to win and it was nice to do a job for the team."

Phoebe Litchfield made her intentions clear after SunRisers were asked to bat, the Aussie opener racing to 27 from 12 deliveries to leapfrog Sophia Dunkley at the top of the competition's run-scoring chart.

An electrifying innings was brought to a halt after Litchfield miscued a drag down from Mady Villiers but Bryony Smith (17 off 16) and Lauren Winfield-Hill (20 off 15) kept the scoreboard ticking.

Sports.title: Levy goes up against Spurs owners to buy London's NBA Europe team
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy is vying with a consortium including current Spurs' owners, the Lewis family, to buy NBA Europe's London-based team.

Sky News has revealed that the Lewises are part of a consortium, led by the Checketts family, which has submitted an offer as part of the ongoing auction.

The Checketts have owned or invested in professional sports franchises including Major League Soccer team Real Salt Lake and the NHL's St Louis Blues.

The third leg of the consortium is the Eccles family, who own shares in Burnley FC and Spanish side Espanyol along with the Checketts.

Sky News has previously reported Levy's involvement in a consortium including Liberty Global and MSP Sports Capital, a former backer of McLaren Racing, which is also among the contenders for the NBA London team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol examines where Daniel Levy was 'pushed' out of his role as Spurs chairman

London has rapidly become most highly prized of the 12 new NBA Europe outfits, with other teams based in cities such as Berlin, Manchester, Milan, Munich, Paris and Rome.

The NBA wants to generate billions of dollars by selling the rights to the teams, with the first transactions expected in the coming weeks.

Wealthy US families and investors are increasingly buying stakes in sports teams in the UK, especially in football.

Levy left his role as Spurs executive chairman in September 2025 after nearly 25 years in the job.

While the official communication from Spurs and Levy was that he had "stepped down" from the role, it was widely understood that the decision was taken out of his hands.

Sports.title: Inter Milan in talks over Spurs and England defender Spence
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Inter Milan over the sale of Djed Spence.

Inter believe a total package of £30m could be enough to get a deal done and Spurs are understood to be willing to sell if they receive an acceptable offer.

Spence's opportunities could be limited at Spurs this season with Destiny Udogie and Andy Robertson also competing for the left-back position and the ever-present Pedro Porro the clear first choice on the right.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Spence's brilliant cameo off the bench against Norway, England fans Ben Cipolla and Dan Lucas came up with a new song for the full-back titled 'Total Eclipse of Djed Spence'

Inter want to bring in a new player who can operate as a wing-back.

Spence has been high on their list all summer and Inter are now turning their attention to the Spurs man after struggling to strike a deal for Al Ittihad's Moussa Diaby.

De Zerbi: Spurs aren't done in the transfer window

Roberto de Zerbi maintains Tottenham are "not finished yet" in the transfer market as they look to build a competitive Premier League squad again.

Having only avoided relegation on the final day of last season, Spurs have spent already spent around £237m - with the club's transfer record broken twice in deals for Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tottenham Hotspur head coach Roberto De Zerbi tells the Men in Blazers Network that he expects to make more signings this summer (Pictures: Men in Blazers Network)

Dutch defender Jan Paul van Hecke also arrived from Brighton for £52m, while Martin Dubravka, Robertson and Marcos Senesi signed on as free agents.

With Micky van de Ven having also committed his long-term future to the club, there is genuine hope Spurs will soon be challenging at the other end of the table.

"In the transfer market, we have not finished yet [with] the players who will arrive," De Zerbi said, speaking to the Men in Blazers Network.

"We are looking forward to start another season with, I don't know [different] ambitions, but with different results."

De Zerbi continued: "The club has been great because they closed [deals for] very, very important players. I think we have not finished yet.

"Okay, we spent money, but the other clubs made the same or more in the past. To compete in the Premier League, you need first [the] level of the players.

"The ambition of the owner of the club, of the board, of the people who decide behind me are very important and very high, so we have to find the condition to build a strong team, a stronger team than the last seasons, to compete again for the top of the table."

Sports.title: Unbeaten star Bow Echo in shock retirement after setback
Sports.content:
Bow Echo has been retired from racing after the shock news that George Boughey's unbeaten star has suffered a setback in training.

Having won the 2000 Guineas, the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Sussex Stakes this season, Bow Echo was being lined up for Sunday's Prix Jacques le Marois.

Announcing the surprise news on his X account, Boughey said: "It is with great disappointment that we have to announce that Bow Echo has had a setback and will be retired from racing.

"It has been the honour of a lifetime to train a horse like Bow Echo. He has given us some extraordinary days and taken everyone involved on a journey we will never forget.

"To retire unbeaten, having won the 2000 Guineas, St James's Palace Stakes and Sussex Stakes says everything about what an exceptional racehorse he has been.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bow Echo and Gstaad served up a thriller in the St James's Palace Stakes on day one of Royal Ascot

"Bow Echo's remarkable story began with his owner-breeder, the late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid and it is a great sadness that he was not here to see what a lifetime of breeding was able to produce.

"Bow Echo's unbelievable constitution and extraordinary ability have set him apart. We will all miss seeing him at home and on the racecourse but we are incredibly excited for his next chapter and in time, to see a new generation of his progeny on the racecourse."

Sports.content:
Chelsea have made a new enquiry about signing Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly.

The Blues have a long-term interest in the midfielder and have made another check on his availability following Arsenal's signing of Bruno Guimaraes.

However, Arsenal do not want to sell Lewis-Skelly to a local rival and a team they may have to compete with for the top places this season. Chelsea were linked with Lewis-Skelly in January.

It is questionable whether United would be able to do any more significant deals should they make a move for Lewis-Skelly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking in May, Lewis-Skelly said celebrating with the fans meant everything as Arsenal showcased the Premier League trophy around north London

This is amid a market of high prices for central-midfield players this summer, although he can play both positions.

Last season, Arsenal kept their squad together despite a big spend. They want to be ambitious again this summer - but there is an acceptance there will have to be sales.

Players like Ethan Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly would represent pure profit.

Analysis: Would Arsenal be right to sell Lewis-Skelly?

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

"Pure profit" wrote Myles Lewis-Skelly on his Instagram page as Arsenal celebrated the Premier League title. Reading between the lines, it was message over his future.

Despite posing with the Premier League title in May, Lewis-Skelly had a very difficult campaign. Fully fit the whole season, he made just one Premier League start before Christmas - by the start of May he had only managed three.

Many fans felt it was right for Arsenal to move Lewis-Skelly on as the sale of an academy graduate would bring a 'pure profit' funds into the club - hence the message on Instagram.

But everything changed in May, Mikel Arteta put Lewis-Skelly in a previously unused midfield role for a crucial title run-in game against Fulham, and Arsenal got some life back into their team.

With Martin Zubimendi fading in terms of fitness and form - and Arsenal struggling against the Man City title race momentum - Lewis-Skelly was Man of the Match in the 3-0 win that put them back on track for the title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Monday Night Football, Thierry Henry analysed Myles Lewis Skelly's outstanding midfield performance against Fulham.

Lewis-Skelly did not leave the midfield for the rest of the run-in - including the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

From third choice left-back to playing in Arsenal's biggest game in 20 years, Lewis-Skelly had kick-started his Arsenal career again. But now the question marks have returned.

The £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes has threatened his role in the Arsenal midfield. The Gunners' two most expensive players are now the Brazilian and Declan Rice.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes come face-to-face for the first time after the Brazilian made his move from Newcastle to the Premier League champions.

For two midfield positions, Arsenal have Rice, Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Five does not go into two, so does something - or someone in this instance - have to give?

Ever since his breakthrough last year, Lewis-Skelly has become a fan favourite at Arsenal. He has showed his ability in both midfield and left-back - it is worth remembering he played 180 minutes in defence as Arsenal beat Real Madrid in the Champions League in 2025.

There are valid reasons for Arsenal keeping a hold on Lewis-Skelly, particularly given the amount of minutes key midfielder Rice has played over the past year.

The 27-year-old played in all but two of the Premier League, Champions League and Carabao Cup games between January 1 and the end of the season.

Image: Minutes played by Arsenal players in midfield

By the time Rice got to the World Cup, England manager Thomas Tuchel admitted the midfielder was in "a lot of pain". Rice was substituted regularly during the World Cup - something that very rarely happens in an Arsenal shirt.

The sheer amount of minutes he has played means Arsenal cannot rely on the midfielder to just carry on running through the barriers. If Rice is to be rotated more often, then that opens the door for Lewis-Skelly to continue playing.

But on the flip side, Arsenal have Zubimendi and Merino as options for Rice rotation. And with Arsenal needing to address others areas and showing a need to sell better - their record transfer sale is still Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's £35m move to Liverpool in 2017 - then Lewis-Skelly's future opens up a conundrum.

Arteta said important decisions will need to be made this summer to take the team to another level. But a popular academy graduate ends up at a Premier League rival, then that is not just an important decision - it's a controversial one.

Sports.title: Arsenal to retain title? Liverpool above Man Utd? Sky Sports predicted table revealed
Sports.content:
Will Arsenal retain the title? What's in store for Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea under their new managers? And which teams are going to be relegated?

As the new Premier League season draws closer, featuring 215 games to be shown live on Sky Sports, we've fired up the Sky Sports supercomputer to predict the final table.

Find out where your team finishes as we take a look at the risers and fallers in Between the Lines, the Sky Sports strand unpicking the data behind the biggest stories in football.

Arsenal top, Man Utd fourth

Our predicted table, which is based on 10,000 simulations and factors historic performance, transfer business and betting odds, has Arsenal as champions for a second year running.

The Gunners, champions for the first time in 22 years, are tipped to become only the fourth side in Premier League history to retain the crown after Manchester United, Manchester City, and Chelsea.

Their expected points total of 85.2 is almost identical to their title-winning 85-point haul last season and puts them nearly four points clear of Manchester City, who are predicted to be runners-up again as they begin a new era following Pep Guardiola's departure.

City, who have signed Elliot Anderson for a club-record £116m fee, are predicted to finish closer to Arsenal than last season, when they lagged seven points behind. The supercomputer also expects improvement from Liverpool, where Andoni Iraola has taken over following a fifth-placed finish under Arne Slot.

The Reds are predicted to climb two places to third, with an expected points total of 76.8, putting them just ahead of Manchester United, who are predicted to drop a place to fourth despite finishing last season strongly under Michael Carrick.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Champions Arsenal unveiled new £75m signing Bruno Guimaraes

Chelsea, whose list of summer signings includes the £117m they paid for Morgan Rogers, as well as a new manager in Xabi Alonso, are predicted to climb five places to fifth, ahead of sixth-placed Spurs, who are tipped to climb 11 places following a summer of transfer spending.

Aston Villa are predicted to drop out of the Champions League places and finish seventh, with Bournemouth, Brighton and Brentford completing the predicted top half.

Promoted trio doomed? Forest at risk?

At the other end of the table, the Sky Sports supercomputer predicts newly-promoted sides Coventry, Ipswich and Hull will go straight back down to the Championship.

Frank Lampard's Coventry are tipped to mount the strongest survival challenge, with an expected points total only fractionally lower than Nottingham Forest's.

Forest, 16th-placed finishers last term, have appointed former Crystal Palace boss Oliver Glasner as their new head coach but are predicted to finish a place below his old club in 17th.

Newcastle are also expected to endure another difficult season. The Magpies slumped to a disappointing 12th-placed finish last term. Following a turbulent summer in which they have sold key players Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon and replaced Eddie Howe with Matthias Jaissle, they are predicted to come 13th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matthias Jaissle talks about Newcastle's new era after replacing Eddie Howe

The only positive for Newcastle is that they are predicted to finish ahead of rivals Sunderland, who will come 15th this season, according to the Sky Sports supercomputer, despite achieving an historic seventh-placed finish last season.

Everton, up from 13th to 11th, are the only team in our bottom half with a predicted position for the new season higher than their actual finishing position last term. The other spots in the bottom half are taken by Fulham, in 12th, and Leeds, in 14th.

Sports.title: Van Veen asks for help as bags stranded in Paris
Sports.content:
Gian van Veen has taken to social media to ask for help with his bags stuck in Paris ahead of the New Zealand Darts Masters in Auckland this weekend.

Van Veen, runner-up to Luke Littler in the 2026 World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace, has already arrived in Auckland for the event - but his gear has not.

Sports.title: Djed Spence nears Tottenham exit with Inter in talks over £25.6m move
Sports.content:
Tottenham are prepared to allow Djed Spence to join Inter, with the England defender expected to cost around €30m (£25.6m).

Spence – who started four games for England at the World Cup, including the semi-final against Argentina – has fallen further down the pecking order at Spurs after the arrival of Andy Robertson from Liverpool. He signed a new four-year contract in north London at the start of last season but is believed to be keen on joining the Italian champions, with Destiny Udogie and Pedro Porro expected to be Roberto De Zerbi’s preferred full-backs this season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Talks are ongoing over a fee for the 26-year-old as Inter search for a replacement for Denzel Dumfries, who joined Real Madrid this summer. But personal terms are not believed to be an issue and an agreement is likely to be reached that will see Inter pay only slightly more than the £20m fee Spurs paid to sign Spence from Middlesbrough in 2022.

Inter also held talks with Tottenham over a potential move for Cristian Romero but the Argentina defender looks set to join Atlético Madrid for a fee of €40m. They have yet to agree a fee but Romero is expected to move to La Liga despite interest from elsewhere, including Premier League champions Arsenal.

On Monday, Spurs – who have spent almost £240m this summer on new players, including Sandro Tonali for a club record £92.5m, confirmed that Mickey van de Ven has signed a new five-year contract. “It’s clear the direction the club wants to go in and I want to be a part of it. I’m excited about what’s to come,” said the Netherlands defender.

Meanwhile, Crystal Palace are in talks to re-sign Evann Guessand on a season-long loan from Aston Villa. The Côte d’Ivoire forward spent the second half of last season at Selhurst Park and was part of the side that won the Conference League in May, although Palace decided not to take up an option to sign him earlier in the summer. The south London club are also expected to complete deals for Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise for £21m and Xavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake for £11m.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to Manchester United as left-back solution
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to Manchester United as a potential left-back option, with Arsenal wishing to recoup some of the £75m paid to Newcastle for Bruno Guimarães.

Chelsea, it is understood, have also been made aware of the 19-year-old’s availability. Lewis-Skelly won the Premier League under Mikel Arteta last term, but whether the west London club will make a move for him is unclear.

Lewis-Skelly, who made only five league starts and 36 appearances in all competitions in 2025-26, signed a five-year contract last summer. His prospective price is thought to be in the region of £45m.

This is within the range of finance United have spent so far this summer, after Youri Tielemans’s £35m move from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos’s arrival for £48m plus £2m of add-ons from Chelsea.

Newcastle’s Lewis Hall remains of prime interest for United but, after losing Guimarães, Sandro Tonali to Tottenham, and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, the new Newcastle manager, Matthias Jaissle, is intent the 21-year-old England international does not also depart

RB Leipzig’s 28-year-old left-back David Raum is another in the position United may assess.

Chelsea have already had a busy summer in the market, having spent over £300m on a raft of new signings. Maxence Lacroix and Marco Palestra have been brought in to bolster the centre and right of the defence, respectively, while Morgan Rogers became the club’s record signing at a cost of £117m.

But Xabi Alonso’s side have a hole on the left of their defence after Marc Cucurella’s £52m move to Real Madrid. The 20-year-old Jorrel Hato, who featured for the Netherlands at the World Cup, was Cucurella’s deputy at left-back.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Liverpool, Jeff Bezos and mission creep off the field at Anfield
Sports.content:
THIS MEANS MORE (MONEY)

Far be it for Football Daily to make cheap gags [wait, what? – Football Daily Ed] relating to the involvement of Amazon founder and master of the universe Jeff Bezos in a consortium buying around 30% of Liverpool FC. Will new signings arrive via prompt delivery but end up next door at Everton? How will fans rate the packaging? Etc, etc. There’s also the involvement of Eduardo Saverin, the Facebook co-founder poking his head in. Though long ago unfriended by Mark Zuckerberg, Saverin still ranked No 56 on Forbes’s billionaires list. These are seriously rich men, and among the planet’s chino class, to quote Vladimir Putin, “soccer is popular”. The Geopolitics World Cup posh seats were full of those eyeing up deals on a frontier hardly new to investors from the USA USA USA, but where there may be much more gold to strike. See Gianni Infantino’s misreading of the art of the deal as an, ahem, prime example.

Bezos is no football man, barely known as a sports fan. Links with buying the Seattle Seahawks, his local NFL franchise, were speculative. He is, though, the third richest man in the world, according to appendage-measuring listicles. Amazon’s market value is higher than Brazil’s annual GDP. For certain people, that triggers arousal at the thought of their team being able to buy the biggest and best players in the world. Just imagine if their club was to spend, say, £446m in a single summer. How good would that be?

For others, there is a regrettable mission creep towards a civic institution – one that, despite global fame, cleaves to its local community – being tossed around by venture capitalists. Though that process has been in train since Tom Hicks and George Gillett arrived on Merseyside, full of huckster charm, almost two decades ago. The socialism and collectivism Bill Shankly envisaged for the club he made famous disappeared in the sepia-tinged rearview mirror. Football was a business even back in Shanks’ day but now attracts the richest suits of all; if Bezos is chancing his arm in football, what price Elon Musk or Google tycoon Larry Page are seen wearing the scarf of their chosen club? Oh joy.

Current overlords Fenway Sports Group, who picked up the pieces from impending disaster in 2010, are, yes, a consortium of American venture capitalists. Their existential aim is to make as much loot as possible from an asset purchased for a knockdown price of £300m. It’s gone well. This mooted deal includes Bezos, Saverin and Amit Bhatia, a frontman you may recognise from when QPR fans celebrated their owners being richer than Roman Abramovich. That did not go well. The latest deal would value the club at £4.4bn. High-fives all round, though the doubles and trebles may take time. Liverpool enter the season with an imbalanced squad, unsuited to a manager whose arrival was generally seen as a Good Thing. If football is all about money, even the biggest money cannot solve every problem.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“After careful consideration, we don’t feel it is right to proceed at this time without the necessary preparation in place, but we will remain in conversation with the club and see what is possible in the future” – one wealthy benefactor not entering the game – yet – is Turki Alalshikh, whose bid to buy a controlling interest in Derby will no longer proceed, with the club now off the market.

RECOMMENDED LOOKING

Here’s David Squires on … the masochistic life of a Football League fan.

View image in fullscreen Illustration: David Squires/The Guardian

double quotation mark Having also boycotted the GWC and also being very concerned about the season to come, I sympathise with Ken Muir (yesterday’s Football Daily letters). But at least Hearts know who their manager is. Due to the absurd, months-long FA ‘investigation’ into the manager who’s clearly admitted culpability for the undisputed facts of Spygate, my club, Southampton, is in a horrid limbo. Surely it could have been done and dusted in a couple of weeks and Saints could have planned accordingly. But perhaps the FA blazers were too busy writing their letter of support to Gianni Infantino to worry about destabilising my football club” – Bob Cushion.

double quotation mark ‘It’s 15 years of frustration here at this club,’ says Rangers boss Derek McInnes (yesterday’s Quote of the Day.) Steven Gerrard and the sole object in his managerial trophy cabinet would like a word, Derek” – David Maddock.

It has to be worth a thought, before VAR, PGMOL and Arsenal’s Dark Arts Department™ get to work on the 2026-27 Premier League shenanigans, surely?” – Budgie Wright.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 4: Brentford
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 8th (NB: this is not necessarily John Brewin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 9th

Prospects

If the upward trajectory of the Brentford project continued last season, with Keith Andrews proving a capable replacement for Thomas Frank, it ended with disappointment. On the final day, there was a chance of European football for this season, only for a draw at Anfield to deny the club the opportunity to capitalise on Brighton’s loss to Manchester United, an inferior goal difference meaning they finished ninth rather than eighth. A win would have secured a place in the Europa League. Dango Ouattara’s late headed miss will have been relived many times over the summer.

Perhaps the lack of European football may prove a blessing. Smaller clubs being stretched by a heavier schedule is a story often told, both in physical and financial terms, but the continental football dream will not be far from minds if Brentford’s progress sustains. The loss of Jordan Henderson to Chelsea’s new senior citizens’ collective will be felt more in terms of his leadership qualities than his playing influence; he started 22 matches last season in a midfield where a more youthful energy was preferred.

Can Igor Thiago replicate last season? He did enough to win a World Cup selection for Brazil, but hit flat spots even while making such an impression; he scored once in his team’s final six matches, just when they might have needed him most. He will be supported this season by the experience of Callum Wilson, signed as a free agent, while Jaidon Anthony has joined the forward line from Burnley.

Continuity remains a key tenet, building on the foundations laid by the owner, Matthew Benham, and the long-serving sporting director, Phil Giles, that made and sustained Brentford as a top-division club. Each season of the club’s five in the Premier League has seen peaks and troughs ridden out and further progress made. That has to be the coming season’s expectation.

Off-field picture

The published accounts for 2024-25, Frank’s last in charge, showed a £21m loss that was significant, but relatively small potatoes compared to Premier League peers. The sales of Bryan Mbeumo and Yoane Wissa eased finances last summer, but extra revenue streams are being sought. A public consultation is being carried out in view of hosting six live music events at the Gtech. The stadium is built in a residential area, apartment blocks towering over the stands. A sleeve sponsorship deal was renewed with Cazoo, the west London automobile e-commerce dealership. Indeed, the job website, has replaced the previous, South African betting company that adorned the shirts as the main sponsor.

Owner-fan relationship

Just like his former associate Tony Bloom at Brighton, Benham has provided the analytical expertise and the finance to sustain Brentford’s development. For that, fans who grew up as supporters of one of the capital’s smallest clubs, and those who have been attracted more recently, will be for ever grateful. After last year’s arrival of Gary Lubner and Sir Matthew Vaughn as minority shareholders, Prakash Melwani, investment banker, and Sir Lucian Grainge, music mogul, took similar slices of the pie. A formerly parochial club, one still close to its grassroots support, is now helmed by big-hitters from the business world.

The manager

Andrews showed he is far more than the set-piece specialist he was previously employed as. For the difficult second album, he will be aware that opposing managers and their scouts will be better prepared. An adept media performer, he has explained the relative lack of business with typical calm. “We won’t sign players unless we feel they’ll fit into the fabric of the club and the culture and values that we have as a group of people working together on a daily basis,” he said from a pre-season training camp in Portugal. Having confounded doubts as the rookie manager who ended last season with claims on end-of-season awards he now has to prove it was not beginners’ luck.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen New signing Mamadou Sangaré warming up before Brentford’s 4-2 pre-season friendly victory against Rennes. Photograph: Lucas Bronchart/Icon Sport/Getty Images

When Lens went close to denying Paris Saint-Germain the Ligue 1 title last season, Mamadou Sangaré was at the heart of their midfield. He was named in the division’s team of the season. Brentford’s midfield has lost Henderson and Christian Nørgaard over the last two summers, though Sangaré will offer different strengths. Opta stats from last season showed only Elliot Anderson and Bayer Leverkusen’s Exequiel Palacios averaged more possession regains in Europe’s top five leagues. Brentford are at their best and most effective when pressing hard and high and Sangaré appears ideal. “He adds qualities that we don’t have,” said Andrews of the club-record £35m signing.

Stat attack

Brentford scored 10 set-play goals last season – it was their joint-fewest in a Premier League campaign and only three teams in the division had a worse record. Yet no club in the division was more reliant upon free-kicks, corners and throw-ins to generate shots. They either need to be more productive in open play or more efficient with their set pieces. Both wouldn’t go amiss.

Set for a breakthrough

To follow Thiago’s successful signing from Belgium, Kaye Furo was bought from Club Brugge in January. Making his debut as Macclesfield were negotiated in the FA Cup in February, he made one Premier League appearance, in May against West Ham. As has been customary at Brentford for new additions, he may have to wait for his turn, particularly with those experienced additions to the forward line. Brentford’s first-mover advantage via analytics and scouting remains widely admired and has delivered more hits than misses to help finance further dealings. Kaye is the son of Furo Iyenemi, who captained Nigeria at the 2000 Olympics.

World Cup impact

The now-departed Henderson played a patrician role within the England squad. Kristoffer Ajer, whose Norway team were beaten in the quarter-finals by England, travelled furthest in the tournament of those who remain. Ajer’s header hit the crossbar in those frantic final moments in Atlanta. To get there, Norway pulled off an historic victory over Brazil, where Thiago was an unused substitute, having made his single, ineffective appearance in the opening 1-1 draw with Morocco. Aaron Hickey’s participation was just as brief, confined to Scotland’s grinding opening win over Haiti before succumbing to injury, unable to contribute as the campaign lurched into familiar disappointment.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Nottingham Forest seal £34m deal for Sporting’s Diomande
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have signed Côte d’Ivoire defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting for an undisclosed fee, reported to be £34.2m.

The 22-year-old centre-half, who featured in the Côte d’Ivoire’s World Cup squad, has agreed a four-year deal with Forest, who have an option for a further year.

Forest’s chief football officer, George Syrianos, said: “He has fantastic experience for a defender of his age. Playing a crucial role in title winning teams and going into the latter stages of the Champions League puts him in a great position to integrate well here at Forest.”

Diomande began his professional career in Denmark with FC Midtjylland and after joining Sporting in January 2023 he made 132 appearances for the Portuguese club in all competitions.

He played a key role in Sporting’s run in the Champions League last season, starting both legs in their quarter-final defeat by Arsenal, and also played the full 90 minutes in Côte d’Ivoire’s World Cup group win against Curaçao.

Fulham have signed midfielder Shea Charles from Southampton for a reported £30m fee, which would be a record deal for a Northern Ireland international. Charles, 22, has agreed a five-year contract, with a club option to extend by a further 12 months.

“It’s a great club, with a really good vision – the manager [Alvaro Arbeloa] explained that to me. To be here is a massive privilege,” Charles said. “I hope to really kickstart my Premier League career. At such a good club as well, it’s perfect for me, and hopefully perfect for the fans as well.”

Filip Jorgensen has joined Strasbourg on a season-long loan from Chelsea. The 24-year-old goalkeeper arrived at Stamford Bridge in 2024 from Villarreal and has made 36 appearances for the Blues.

Jorgensen started all but one of Chelsea’s games in the Conference League last year and featured 12 times in all competitions. He will now spend the 2026-27 campaign with Strasbourg, who finished eighth in Ligue 1 last season.

Sports.title: League Two 2026-27 preview: the contenders, hopefuls and strugglers
Sports.content:
Contenders

Salford meekly lost the playoff final and that was the end of days for Karl Robinson as he was sacked. Peter Cklamovski was not the obvious replacement, but the Australian left behind the Malaysia national side for a crack at League Two with the rebranded Ammies, who are back in their traditional orange. Macaulay Langstaff has arrived with the task of providing the goals to finally get Salford up and few would bet against the striker.

Chesterfield fell short in the playoffs, too, but Paul Cook remains one of the best managers at this level, although the loss of Armando Dobra could be significant. Securing the veteran forward Andy Cook was important for Grimsby as they seek to push on and his influence could be telling if he plays enough games. Lee Grant did not get much chance to prove himself at Huddersfield so will be desperate to do so at Walsall, especially after a promising start by knocking Championship side Bristol City out of the EFL Cup. The former goalkeeper will be hoping he is the man to ensure the Saddlers do not stop playing in winter, as has been the case in recent years.

Of those who have dropped down, Rotherham are the more intriguing bet, having brought in Steve McClaren as director of football and Alex Bruce as head coach in an attempt to revitalise the club. Losing Sam Nombe was a blow, but his transfer fee should allow investment. Jon Brady knows what he is doing and could do nothing to keep Port Vale up, but arguably has the most complete squad at this level with Max Watters and Kyle Dempsey standout summer signings.

View image in fullscreen Rotherham will hope to utilise the experience of their director of football Steve McClaren to bolster their chances of promotion into League One. Photograph: WhiteRosePhotos/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

Hopefuls

An end‑of‑season slump kept Crewe out of the playoffs last time round, but the returns of Luke Offord and Joe White provide much‑needed quality. Barnet were two points off eighth having returned to the EFL and have kept their developing squad together – apart from Ryan Glover who was sold to Stockport – to give Dean Brennan real belief that his side can improve. Oldham made a steady return to the fourth tier and have added the guarantee of Elliott Nevitt’s goals alongside Oliver Norburn, who was a key member of the Notts County side that went up from this division.

Colin Kazim-Richards has his feet fully under the table at Crawley and has overseen one of their traditional busy summers in an attempt to avoid a relegation battle. The former Sunderland goalkeeper Vito Mannone was an eye‑catching signing, while the talented Malcolm Ebiowei will be aiming to turn his career around. If these two shine, it could make them a surprise package. Relegation and problems off the pitch have put Exeter on a downward spiral, which does not look like being arrested without further incomings. “Absolute tinpot garbage” was Ian Holloway’s view of Swindon’s friendly performance against Bristol City, which suggests the team still have levels to go. Gareth Ainsworth wants high‑pressing Gillingham to maintain energy levels over the course of the campaign to give them an outside chance of challenging.

Quick Guide PFA takes EFL to high court over changes to salary cap rules in League One Show The Professional Footballers’ Association has begun high court proceedings against the English Football League over changes to the salary cap rules in League One. The division’s clubs approved changes to the existing Salary Cost Management Protocol (SCMP) rules in May, with “the aim of reducing losses and the reliance on owner funding in the division”. The changes reduced the amount League One clubs will be allowed to spend on wages from 60% to 50%, with manager salaries also now to be included in SCMP calculations. But the players’ union believes all parties within the Professional Football Negotiating and Consultative Committee (PFNCC) – the Premier League, EFL, PFA and the Football Association – were not properly consulted. A PFA spokesperson said: “The PFA have begun high court action against the EFL in relation to new wage restriction rules adopted by clubs in League One and introduced this season. “We believe that the process through which clubs have voted to bring in these new measures, which will artificially restrict and tighten what clubs can spend on player wages, was not in line with the consultation and agreement process required by the EFL’s membership (alongside the PFA, FA and Premier League) of the Professional Football Negotiating and Consultative Committee (PFNCC).” In response, the EFL said it is “concerned and disappointed at the position adopted by the PFA”. The EFL said: “The proposed changes have been discussed at length through the PFNCC process, including with the PFA, and the EFL has taken those discussions into account. “The PFA has argued that the league cannot implement the changes unless there is full agreement through the PFNCC. The league does not accept that the PFA’s position is correct.” The EFL added: “The EFL will continue to engage constructively with the PFA and other stakeholders. But it cannot ignore the financial pressures facing clubs or accept further delay when the risks to the game are increasing. Our priority is clear: a fair, competitive and financially sustainable league system that protects clubs, players, supporters and communities over the long term.” Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

George Burley’s son-in-law Chris Hogg joined Northampton in May for his first managerial role and, after sunning himself in Greece, is primed to test himself, but the Cobblers may rue the departure of Cameron McGeehan as they aim to rebuild after relegation. Gavin Cowan transformed Shrewsbury from no-hopers to comfortably staying up but he faces a tricky second album.

John Terry is not the Colchester owner, as the sale of the club rumbles on without a solution. Steve Evans will ensure Bristol Rovers are competitive, but whether that means they can push themselves higher than 14th place last season remains to be seen.

Strugglers

The promoted teams start on the backfoot after managerial changes, as Rochdale lost Jimmy McNulty, while York decided to sack Stuart Maynard midway through preseason, much to the consternation of the fans. Diligence in recruitment, however, gives them optimism, especially Dale bringing back Cian Hayes.

Tranmere survived by a couple of points last time round but will be hoping for an uplift under Darrell Clarke, who has persuaded Will Vaulks and the former Watford winger Tom Ince that Prenton Park is a sensible place to continue their careers. Newport County were also forced into a change in the dugout when Christian Fuchs decided Rodney Parade was not the place he wanted to call home having kept the team up, leaving the club in flux as Chris Todd oversaw preparations for the campaign. The Exiles brought in plenty of experience in the shape of Harrison Biggins and Christian Doidge to strengthen the squad.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The inexperienced Matt Lawlor is set for a challenging first full season in charge of Fleetwood, who are boosted by the signing of Andy Cannon from Wrexham. Steve Cotterill revitalised Cheltenham almost a year ago, but five of their first six summer signings were relegated in May, which does not inspire confidence. After finishing comfortably in midtable, Accrington Stanley may not fear the drop and Cole Stockton is a clever signing but there is a nagging doubt about the club’s efficacy.

View image in fullscreen Managerial inexperience may prove challenging for Matt Lawlor (left) who has much to prove in his first full season at Fleetwood Town. Photograph: Phil Oldham/Shutterstock

Ones to watch

Maldini Kacurri, Grimsby, 20 After starting last season on loan at doomed National League side Morecambe, the Albania international may have wondered if life outside Arsenal was really for him. The defender shone when he stepped up to League Two with Grimsby, guided by David Artell, proving himself capable of coping with the physicality in the lower tiers.

Patrick Mlynarski, Crewe, 18 A Wales youth international, the recently-turned 18-year-old is now in his first year as a professional. The winger made his debut in the EFL Trophy last season, but is yet to feature in the league. Previously part of Everton’s academy, Mylnarski is skilful and powerful, playing on the left, possessing the ability to cut in or beat defenders on the outside.

Will Gray, Shrewsbury, 17 The midfielder made four starts last season and signed his first professional contract in the summer. His manager, Gavin Cowan, has praised his mentality and ability to keep things simple in the centre of the park.

Sports.title: Chelsea face Real Sociedad in WCL third qualifying round with riches at stake
Sports.content:
Chelsea will face Real Sociedad in the Women’s Champions League’s third qualifying round, needing a victory over two legs to earn a place in the main league phase of the competition.

The 2021 runners-up and six-time European semi-finalists are taking part in the qualifying stage by virtue of their disappointing third-placed finish in the Women’s Super League last term – their lowest league finish since 2019 – and they will be the favourites against the Spanish side.

Chelsea could have faced Ajax, Inter, Eintracht Frankfurt or the Austrian side St Polten. They were unable to meet the big-name sides such as Real Madrid, Wolfsburg, Juventus or Paris Saint-Germain at this stage because of seedings. Sonia Bompastor’s side will hope to join Arsenal and Manchester City in the main phase of the competition.

The potential financial implications of missing out on qualification are significant. All 18 clubs that take part in the league phase will receive a guaranteed minimum of €505,000, plus a further €60,000 for every league phase fixture they win and €20,000 for every draw, as well as prize money ranging from €10,000 to €180,000 depending on where they finish in the table, rising by €10,000 per position.

Additionally, the eventual champions would receive €1,050,000 in prize money across the course of the knockout phase – including €500,000 specifically for winning the final – as there are six-figure sums on offer for each knockout-phase fixture.

Chelsea will be at home for the first leg, which is scheduled to be played on 26 August, with the second leg in Spain scheduled for 2 September, three days before Chelsea’s WSL season opener, which is at home against Aston Villa on 5 September.

Chelsea have been strong contenders for the European title in recent years, reaching the semi-finals in three of the past four campaigns, but they lost to their rivals Arsenal in a dramatic quarter-final last term.
