TUESDAY: Man City step up chase for Chelsea's Pedro Neto

Sports.title: Awkward moment footballer is blanked by his girlfriend dubbed 'Uruguay's Kim Kardashian' after swooping in for a kiss at his transfer unveiling... before hilariously trying to style it out
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A footballer hoping for a smooch on one of the proudest days of his career was left with lonely lips after his girlfriend blanked and abandoned him on stage.

Uruguay striker Luciano Rodriguez was celebrating his loan move to Brazilian giants Cruzeiro alongside his girlfriend Anto Ciavaglia.

But just as he leaned in for a kiss in front of the cameras, Ciavaglia – who has been dubbed the 'Uruguayan Kim Kardashian' – turned and left him stone cold.

Rodriguez's smile vanished and he was forced to awkwardly stand on his own for a few seconds before running his hand through his hair.

Footage of the awkward moment has gone viral on social media, and Ciavaglia has had to quell any talk of a rift between them.

The 23-year-old model, who has more than 170,000 Instagram followers, said: 'When I entered, I greeted him and when I left, I was very nervous.

Uruguay striker Luciano Rodriguez was blanked and abaondoned by his girlfriend as he went searching for a kiss upon joining Cruzeiro

The forward, 23, tired to style out the awkward moment by running his hand through his hair

His girlfriend, Anto Ciavaglia, who has been dubbed the 'Uruguayan Kim Kardashian,' said she had simply been nervous and did not mean to disrespect him

'The moment overwhelmed me and I preferred to give him space.

'There was no disrespect or anything like what they are trying to make it seem like.'

One clip has been seen more than 4.6 million times.

In more footage from the unveiling, Rodriguez's mother was seen breaking down in tears as she sat next to Ciavaglia, no doubt proud of her son.

Rodriguez, 23, has plenty to celebrate in his career. The striker has been capped five times for his country but narrowly missed out on a place in Uruguay's World Cup squad.

He has also won the Under-20s World Cup and the Uruguayan Premier Division when he was at Liverpool Montevideo in 2023.

After two seasons in Brazil with Bahia, he switched to Neom in the Saudi Pro League last campaign but only scored six goals in 30 games. He has now linked up with Cruzeiro on loan with a reported £14.95million buy option.

At Cruzeiro, he links up with former Leeds forward Luis Sinisterra and ex-West Brom man Matheus Pereira.

His girlfriend, Anto Ciavaglia, was reported by Uruguayan newspaper El Pais to have been dubbed the 'Uruguayan Kim Kardashian' in 2021.

Commenting on the comparison, she told the outlet: 'It's super cute because I love her. I'm a huge fan.'

Sports.title: Arne Slot reveals why he withdrew from Netherlands job talks less than THREE MONTHS after being sacked by Liverpool
Sports.content:
Arne Slot reveals why he withdrew from Netherlands job talks less than THREE MONTHS after being sacked by Liverpool

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Liverpool manager Arne Slot has revealed he turned down the chance to manage the Netherlands because he wants to remain in club football.

The Premier League-winning manager was in negotiations to take over the national team of his homeland after being sacked as Liverpool boss in the summer, but withdrew from the race.

Ronald Koeman had departed following the World Cup, and Slot was the favoured replacement by many as he found himself out of work.

Some reports suggested Slot had turned down the opportunity because of potential salary and contract length, but the 47-year-old has released a statement revealing the true reason.

'Over the past few weeks, and particularly the past few days, various reports have appeared regarding the vacancy at the Dutch national team, suggesting that I had withdrawn from the process after lengthy negotiations, including regarding salary and contract duration,' Slot said via Dutch publication Voetbal International. 'That speculation is incorrect. We simply never reached that stage of the talks.

'At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day. Something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team. And why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like.'

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (left) has revealed why he turned down the opportunity to manage the Netherlands

'It would be a great honor to represent my country as national coach one day. However, this was not the right moment for me.'

Slot was sacked by Liverpool at the end of May, just one year after the Dutchman had led the Reds to the Premier League title.

His dismissal came after Liverpool finished fifth in the Premier League at the end of a campaign where Slot oversaw 20 defeats in all competitions.

Slot also came under pressure from supporters and saw several key players – such as the now-departed Mohamed Salah – speak out about the playing style.

He was sacked following a review into Liverpool’s troubled season that was led by Richard Hughes and Michael Edwards, chief executive of football at the club’s owner, Fenway Sports Group.

Prior to joining Liverpool, Slot had led Feyenoord to the Eredivisie title and the Dutch Cup, while they also finished as runners-up in the Conference League.

He was linked with a move to Al-Ahli in Saudi Arabia after Newcastle appointed Matthias Jaissle, but turned down that opportunity too.

Sports.title: How Ronald Araujo jumped at the chance to join Liverpool - and why 'humble' and 'old school' defender solves three problems for Andoni Iraola, reveals LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
How Ronald Araujo jumped at the chance to join Liverpool - and why 'humble' and 'old school' defender solves three problems for Andoni Iraola, reveals LEWIS STEELE

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

If Liverpool fans have had one gripe this summer, it is that their long search for a Mohamed Salah replacement has dragged on and on, with drawn-out sagas for first Yan Diomande and now Bradley Barcola.

But as for the two players they have signed, it's been as easy as uno, dos, tres. Spanish World Cup winner Victor Munoz arrived for £34.5million from Osasuna in June, and yesterday it was the turn of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo.

It is understood the Reds only made contact with the Uruguay international’s camp last Wednesday. From that point on, Araujo only had one thing on his mind: make this move happen.

Araujo spoke to new Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola and was immediately sold on the move, a view furthered by talks with sporting director Richard Hughes. This was an opportunity he could not pass up – he has always wanted to play in the Premier League.

He wanted the move so much, in fact, that he took a pay cut to make it happen. While Liverpool will cover his salary in full, Araujo will not receive as much as he did at Barcelona.

If the season-long loan goes well, the Reds have agreed a £47.1million fee to make it permanent.

Ronald Araujo's loan move from Barcelona will help to ease Liverpool's defensive crisis

The versatile Araujo can cover at both centre-half and full back and will likely be thrown straight in by Andoni Iraola

There have been reservations among some fans about Araujo's ability and reliability but the positives of this move far outweigh the negatives.

First, his arrival alleviates a gaping hole in Liverpool’s back line – one that Iraola had identified as a problem area given a multitude of defensive injuries.

Just eight minutes into the first pre-season friendly, Joe Gomez limped off with a muscle injury and he will not be available for the beginning of the Premier League season.

Young duo Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni also remain sidelined, while Virgil van Dijk is 35 and only contracted to the end of the coming season. Losing Ibrahima Konate, the experienced French defender who joined Real Madrid for nothing, was a major blow.

Jacquet is set to resume full training this week, it is understood, while Leoni is in the final stage of rehabilitation after missing the best part of a year with a ligament problem. Jacquet has also not played since February so, even if the pair were fit, they will need a bedding-in period.

Araujo, who has played 213 times for Barcelona and won LaLiga on three occasions, can help the duo settle slowly rather than be thrown in at the deep end.

The other big positive about Araujo's arrival is that he can fill in at right back, another problem area given Conor Bradley’s long-term injury.

Need cover for Jacquet or Leoni? Step up, Araujo. Need cover for Bradley or Jeremie Frimpong? Step up, Araujo.

Experts in Spain say Araujo is an old-school defender who likes to get stuck in

Araujo (pictured with wife Abigail and his daughters Aitana and Adara) is a family man whose favourite pastime is spending time with his loved ones

Sources say the 27-year-old is not the most vocal of players in the dressing room but he has a strong presence and gains the respect of team-mates. Instead of hiding when times get tough, he is said to be keen to get involved and step up.

He remains humble and has always stayed in touch with friends from back home in Uruguay. A fan of firing up his barbecue on days off, Araujo is a family man whose favourite pastime is spending time with his loved ones.

With those LaLiga titles under his belt, to go with two Copa del Rey winner's medals, Araujo knows what it takes to win. He has also featured twice in the team of the season in Spain.

But his journey to this point has not always been straightforward. The glare of life at Barcelona has caused Araujo issues with anxiety at points. Several poor performances led to his family receiving death threats. He took a break from football in late 2025.

In an interview with The Athletic before the World Cup, he revealed: ‘I’m going to tell you something that might come as a surprise. Even though I haven’t played that many minutes, this has been the season I’ve learnt the most.

‘I’ve grown a lot mentally. I’ve learnt to be a better husband, a better father, to see things differently, to put things into perspective. People think that because we’re footballers and earn a lot of money, we don’t have any worries, but we do.

‘A lot of things happen in the world of football, and they build up, causing you stress. You can play on a Wednesday and be the best in the world, while on Saturday you lose and you’re the worst.’

Araujo should be lauded for taking his mental health seriously and stepping away to work on his wellbeing. So too for speaking out so frankly. For the Barcelona captain to do that must be inspiring to other players struggling around the world.

The defender has struggled under the scrutiny of life at Barcelona during recent seasons

He has had troubles on the pitch, too, and his form has been inconsistent at times. He has missed 40 games over the last two seasons through absences, physical or mental, according to Transfermarkt. The defender has also been shown four red cards in his career.

Despite the caveats, Liverpool believe Araujo brings important qualities with his experience, leadership and versatility. A source in Spain told Daily Mail Sport this was ‘100 per cent a top signing’ and discussed Araujo's old-school defensive traits, such as a desire to get stuck in.

He is extremely competitive and enjoys taking responsibility in duels. He is quick, strong in the air and old-fashioned in the sense that he loves the physical side of the game. He has developed his on-the-ball game, too.

Another reason to be cheerful for the Reds is they have ticked off a priority position on their shopping list without spending a fee. It allows them to focus on signing at least one forward.

Araujo’s name was a surprise in a summer where many centre backs have been churned out by the rumour-mill. Tottenham’s Micky van de Ven was strongly linked, while Ezri Konsa of Aston Villa was also said to be one considered.

There was talk of Chelsea’s Josh Acheampong and Maxence Lacroix, then of Crystal Palace, while Club Bruges' Joel Ordonez was a name that never went away after January links.

But that talk is over and it is Araujo who has emerged as solution to Liverpool's defensive crisis.

Sports.title: How England can do the impossible - and fill the hole left by Ben Stokes: The 'burly' all-rounder in the Andrew Flintoff mould, a spinner that Graeme Swann is backing and the teenage freak athlete who caught selectors' eye
Sports.content:
The international retirement of Ben Stokes has left Stephen Fleming and Joe Root with an impossible hole to fill. For 13 years, Stokes was the man England turned to when they needed heroics with the bat or a breakthrough with the ball. His legacy as one of English cricket's finest all-rounders is secured. But who should replace him when the Fleming-Root era begins in earnest in South Africa this winter, and beyond? Should England look to a familiar face with Test experience, or put their faith in a rising star taking their first steps in red-ball cricket? Here Daily Mail Sport examines the runners and riders. Ben Stokes' international retirement has left the new England leadership duo of Stephen Fleming and Joe Root with a major problem to solve

Your browser does not support iframes.

The heir apparent England have already nominated Sam Curran as their No 1 Test all-rounder, which itself sums up the problem. He has been ignored by the selectors since 2021, while his 24 caps have produced underwhelming figures: batting and bowling averages of 24 and 35. And however much his batting has improved in the last few years, it will still be asking a lot of him to balance the side: only four of his 38 Test innings have been above No 8, while his most recent half-century came nearly eight years ago. Curran’s left-arm seamers do offer a variety that England’s attack has often lacked: their last significant left-arm quick, Ryan Sidebottom, played his final Test in January 2010. And there is no doubting his competitive instincts. But he feels like a white-ball player these days: since his last Test cap, he has played only 14 Championship matches for Surrey. And yet Marcus North, England’s new national selector, recently felt able to say: ‘He’s someone that we really value highly and we see playing a role in the future for us as an all-rounder.’ If fit, and depending on conditions, Curran could be drafted in for the third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston. Sam Curran appears to be England's No1 choice to replace Stokes - but the 28-year-old has not played Test cricket since 2021 But is there a stronger candidate? The star all-rounder on the county circuit this summer has been Somerset’s Craig Overton, and it’s not even close. He has scored 548 runs at 45, including centuries against Essex, Sussex and Warwickshire, and taken 33 wickets at 19, including five for 29 to set up a crushing victory over reigning champions Nottinghamshire. Then there was his ridiculous unbeaten 79 off 30 balls to pinch a T20 Blast quarter-final from under Yorkshire’s nose. But there is a reason England haven’t picked him since he won the last of his eight Test caps in the final game of the previous Joe Root era, against West Indies in Grenada: they don’t think he’s quick enough. Worse, England came to the view that he wasn’t even the best cricketer in his family, only for Craig’s twin, Jamie, to announce he was taking an ‘indefinite break’ from Test cricket after last year’s Oval showdown against India. Craig is tall, burly and hits the ball a long way. These are the qualities normally associated with England’s tradition of rabble-rousing all-rounders, from Ian Botham via Andrew Flintoff through to Stokes. But the selectors remain unconvinced. Craig Overton (right) has been the standout all-rounder in the County Championship this year, though England preferred his twin brother Jamie (left) against India in 2025 What about a spin-bowling option? Two names stand out, and both could balance the team by going in at No 7, below Jamie Smith – a bonus not currently provided by Shoaib Bashir, who is a rabbit with a bat and no gazelle in the field. Rehan Ahmed turns 22 on Thursday, but has already played five Tests, all on the subcontinent: 22 wickets at 31, including five on debut in Karachi at the age of 18, is a decent return. His batting brought him five centuries for Leicestershire last summer, but he needs to add a reliable leg-break to his almost-stock googly. James Coles, 22, was named in the T20 squad for the recent series against India, though he didn’t get a game. He has averaged 40 with the bat this season for Sussex and taken 17 wickets at 31 with his left-arm spin, but his stock has dipped a touch after failing to live up to his £390,000 price tag in the Hundred: seven matches have brought him just 44 runs and four wickets for struggling London Spirit. England may take him to Bangladesh for their two-Test series in February. Essex leg-spinner Matt Critchley has good numbers, but turns 30 this week, while Northamptonshire’s Calvin Harrison – arguably the best slip fielder in the country – hasn’t had his best summer with the ball. Sussex off-spinner Jack Carson has an influential fan in Graeme Swann, while Yorkshire’s Dom Bess appears to have drifted from the selectors’ thoughts. Rehan Ahmed turns 22 on Thursday, but has already played five Tests, all on the subcontinent: 22 wickets at 31, including five on debut in Karachi at the age of 18, is a decent return Any other options in county cricket? In Division One, the next-best after Overton is Yorkshire’s George Hill, who has an advocate in England white-ball captain Harry Brook, and has enjoyed a strong summer. But there are concerns over the 25-year-old's lack of pace. The same goes for Warwickshire captain Ed Barnard. The second tier offers several options, but – again – no one with the air speed to trouble the best Test batsmen on a regular basis. Durham’s Ben Raine has averaged 39 with the bat and 17 with the ball this season, but is 34. Ryan Higgins has often held Middlesex together, but operates around 75mph; the same goes for Worcestershire’s Matthew Waite. Kent have high hopes for Ekansh Singh, who scored a century from No 7 for England Under 19s against their Indian counterparts at Chelmsford last summer, while Durham are equally excited about Kasey Aldridge. Yorkshire's George Hill has an advocate in Harry Brook, but England are concerned about his lack of pace Is there really no one in the Botham-Flintoff-Stokes mould? Well… eyebrows were raised by the performance of Caleb Falconer in the Under-19 World Cup final against India at Harare in February. England were chasing a near-impossible 412 after teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi had blasted 175 off 80 balls, and collapsed to 177 for seven in reply. Falconer chose the moment to hit out, thrashing 115 off just 67 deliveries and taking England to a respectable 311. Not yet 20, the South African-born Falconer has already represented England Lions, top-scoring with 45 in a one-day game against his former compatriots at New Road in June. Last month, he hit a century as England Under 19s came close to chasing down 386 in a four-day game. He needs to work on his bustling seamers but is a proper athlete in the field. Watch this space.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle admits club are set for 'transition' season and squad lack leaders as new Toon head coach offers reality check at St James' Park unveiling
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle admits club are set for 'transition' season and squad lack leaders as new Toon head coach offers reality check at St James' Park unveiling

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Matthias Jaissle says he has inherited a ‘vacuum’ of leadership at Newcastle United as he called for new signings and time ahead of what he has labelled a ‘transition’ season.

The 38-year-old German was unveiled at St James’ Park on Tuesday after replacing Eddie Howe, who stood down this month amid concerns over the campaign that awaited.

Newcastle have sold captain Bruno Guimaraes, star players Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon and lost Kieran Trippier since the end of last season. The five incomings so far have no Premier League experience and four are aged 20 or under.

Jaissle wants to add experience – a deal for midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg fell through this week – and he was pressed on the club's loss of four senior players, leaving the squad looking light less than two weeks out from the visit of Liverpool in the Premier League opener.

‘We are in that transition phase,’ he said. ‘The players who have left were great characters, great players, experienced players. This is now a vacuum. We have to adjust something in the squad by signing these profile of players, or other players need to step up and fill these positions and these leadership roles.

‘We are aware of what we need and the squad that we want. Internally, everyone is aware of that, and we are working on the solutions.’

New Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle has warned the club are in for a 'transition' season

Howe’s remit last season was European qualification – the team finished 12th – but Jaissle would not commit to what the hierarchy have asked of him this term, insisting the rebuild needs time.

‘This will not happen overnight, especially when you now have such a big transition phase,’ he said. ‘You need to have a clear goal of where we want to go to. Then, if you have that synergy with the fans, the players and the staff to go there, then I’m pretty sure it will be a successful story. But we need time now. We can only do our best day by day, breaking it down with the goal long ahead.

‘We are ambitious. But it makes no sense to promise you anything, because I don’t know how things look in half a year or one year. What we can control, we will control. Cutting the tasks down on a daily basis, doing the best job, and then we go in the right direction - and that is going to be successful.’

Sports.title: Like father, like son! Freddie Flintoff's 18-year-old son, Rocky, blazes stunning maiden hundred for Lancashire in just 65 balls
Sports.content:
Rocky Flintoff, son of England legend Freddie, enjoyed a day to remember as he struck his maiden hundred for Lancashire.

Playing against Somerset in the Metro Bank One Day Cup, Flintoff, 18, smashed a stunning 123 off just 76 balls as Lancashire racked up a mammoth 443-6 off their 50 overs.

The 18-year-old struck 10 fours and seven sixes as he shone in the blazing sunshine in Taunton.

Flintoff looked in imperious form and brought up his 100 in just 65 balls as he put on a 214-run fourth wicket partnership with former England opener Keaton Jennings, who hit 156.

The middle-order batter was eventually dismissed off the bowling of South African Migael Pretorius, with Archie Vaughan, son of Ashes 2005-winning captain Michael, a former team-mate of Flintoff Snr, taking the catch.

Flintoff made his First-Class and List A debuts as a 16-year-old during the 2024 season, but after missing much of the 2025 campaign through injury, he has been given an opportunity to shine over recent weeks.

Rocky on the attack! 🚀



Flintoff dispatches a four and a six in consecutive balls as he looks to keep upping our run rate!



🌹 #RedRoseTogether pic.twitter.com/dITNQwguZx — Lancashire Cricket (@lancscricket) August 11, 2026

Freddie Flintoff's son Rocky, 18, struck his maiden hundred for Lancashire on Tuesday

Flintoff brought up his century off just 65 balls and hit seven sixes in his incredible innings

With several of Lancashire's more senior batters away at The Hundred, Flintoff has featured in seven of their eight group matches in the One Day Cup and impressed.

After his knock on Tuesday, Flintoff had scored 293 runs across seven innings at an average of 73.25.

That makes him Lancashire's third top run scorer in the competition behind Jennings and their Australian overseas batter Marcus Harris.

Given his age, Flintoff continues to feature regularly for England's Under 19 side, while he also struck a century for the England Lions against a Cricket Australia XI in early 2025, highlighting his prestigious talent.

He is one of a number of famous sons of England's 2005 generation making their way in the cricketing world.

Vaughan, a top-order batter and off-spin bowler, is slightly older than Flintoff at 20, yet he is a regular in Somerset's One Day and First-Class team.

Charlie Harmison, son of former England fast-bowler Steve, is on the books at Durham and featured alongside Flintoff for England's Under 19 side earlier this summer.

Rocky's older brother Corey also enjoyed a short stint with Kent last summer.

Flintoff's feat came against Archie Vaughan, son of his dad's former England captain Michael

When making his debut in the One Day Cup in 2024, Flintoff became Lancashire's youngest ever player at 16 years and 113 days, and he signed a new two-year contract with the club earlier this year.

His father is one of England's most popular and iconic cricketers of all-time, featuring in 79 Tests - including the 2005 and 2009 Ashes series victories - 141 ODIs and seven T20Is.

He was in charge of the England Lions, the team Rocky had featured for, until he stepped down from the role last week.

Sports.title: Man Utd make decision on top transfer target after Myles Lewis-Skelly U-turn
Sports.content:
Man Utd make decision on top transfer target after Myles Lewis-Skelly U-turn

Manchester United are in the market for another central midfielder and also want to add a left-back but do not appear to be considering a move for Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly

View 2 Images Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly could be on the move (Image: (Photo by Marc Atkins/Getty Images))

Manchester United are set to continue their pursuit of Lewis Hall in their search for a new left-back despite once again being offered the chance to sign Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly.

‌



The Red Devils have prioritised midfielders in the transfer window this summer, completing deals for Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. It's understood the club would like to add another central midfielder before the deadline, however, there are other areas which still need strengthening ahead of the upcoming Premier League campaign.

‌



United would ideally like to add another left-back who has the potential to become Luke Shaw's long-term successor at Old Trafford.

‌



Hall has been a priority target despite doubts over whether Newcastle, having already sanctioned significant sales for Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, would consider doing a deal.

Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his preference clear as Man Utd and Chelsea sounded out READ MORE :

Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow READ MORE :

But United's stance hasn't changed according to The Sun, who claim they have no interest in pursuing a deal for Lewis-Skelly.

The Arsenal midfielder has featured prominently for the Premier League champions at left-back and was previously offered to United via an intermediary back in January. At the time, they were understood to be more receptive to a deal, although they were quoted a price of around £60million for the 19-year-old.

‌



Arsenal have grand ambitions to level up the squad that came within a whisker of a Premier League and Champions League double and player sales will be necessary to facilitate further quality signings. As an academy graduate, any funds raised from selling Lewis-Skelly would equate to pure profit, giving Arsenal greater financial flexibility in the market. Chelsea have also been offered the chance to sign Lewis-Skelly.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall is Manchester United's preferred left-back target (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Hall remains United's priority transfer target and, while Newcastle do not want to lose him, the player is keen on moving to Old Trafford, the report adds.

‌



His desire to pursue a new challenge is likely to represent an early headache for the club's new head coach, Matthias Jaissle, who has replaced Eddie Howe at the helm.

Hall has established himself as one of the top left-back's in the Premier League since joining Newcastle from Chelsea back in 2023. The 21-year-old made 30 appearances in the league for Newcastle last term, scoring one goal.

Sports.title: Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem
Sports.content:
Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem

Martin Zubimendi is being linked with the Arsenal exit door after only one year and the signing of Bruno Guimaraes suggests the Spaniard will be shunted down the pecking order

View 4 Images Arsenal signing of Bruno Guimaraes could have a knock on affect on the squad (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

When someone of Bruno Guimaraes' calibre arrives at Arsenal, amid all the fanfare, there will be someone wondering if their time is up.

‌



The Brazilian has just moved to the Emirates for £75million after making it known that the Gunners were the club for him. This is a player who could play for any team in Europe and he will inevitably make Arsenal better.

‌



But if he comes in, that leaves one player having to go out and as part of the fallout reports have emerged that Arsenal have named their price on Martin Zubimendi. That generally only happens for players who could be on the move.

‌



You don't see any prices being quoted for Declan Rice, because he's one of Arsenal's untouchables, if they ever did make such a list. Zubimendi less so and after only a year at Arsenal the Spaniard could be set for a new role, and one he may not enjoy, if he stays.

Its a huge change for a player who, it was well documented, Mikel Arteta had eyed for several years before eventually luring him to London. This was a player who dominated England in the Euro 2024 final, making replacing Rodri look a simple task.

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

But elite clubs only go looking for players in areas where they think they can improve. You hear no noise around Arsenal landing a top class centre-half, because in William Saliba and Gabriel, they have what they need. You hear no noise around Manchester City signing a top tier No 9, because they have Erling Haaland.

‌



Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes showed that they feel they can upgrade in that position. Rice is their talisman but alongside him there's been plenty of contenders. Mikel Merino is one, albeit very versatile, Zubimendi another. Myles Lewis-Skelly may have ambitions to play in that role.

If Zubimendi is to shift from a player who was guaranteed to start to one who isn't, then perhaps the warning signs were there. This is a player who started 34 of 38 games last season - but was benched for three of the final four.

View 4 Images Martin Zubimendi increasingly found himself on the bench towards the end of the season

‌



The Spaniard's minutes were cut and he endured the embarrassment of being subbed on, and then off, by Arteta. That came in the vital win over West Ham with Zubimendi coming on in the 28th minute for the injured Ben White. But his afternoon lasted less than 40 minutes and he was hauled off in the 67th minute for Kai Havertz.

"It is never easy to do that to a player, especially someone with Martin’s quality," Arteta admitted after the game.

Weeks later and Lewis-Skelly, who had been snubbed for much of the season, was picked to play in the Champions League final against PSG. Zubimendi started on the bench, and that's where he would remain for the evening.

‌



Managers can talk all they want about the value and the importance of a player, but what really tells is whether they call upon them come crunch time. With the title in the balance and a European Cup on the line, Zubimendi found himself overlooked.

View 4 Images The Spaniard did claim the Premier League title in his first campaign with Arsenal

When Zubimendi signed from Real Sociedad the club's sporting director, Andrea Berta, claimed: "Martin was a key target for us and we all know that he is a perfect fit for our squad with the high quality he has."

‌



That fit does not look so perfect now following Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes. Arteta has a squad that is the envy of most of Europe, but he'll find that having so many options creates as many problems as solutions it solves.

Arsenal have effectively played with two holding midfielders and a 10, previously Martin Odegaard. The Norwegian too is a man under pressure for his spot. Going on the fact that Rice is the pillar and Guimaraes, the second most expensive player in Arsenal history, will start - where does that leave Zubimendi?

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta has some difficult decisions regarding the make-up of his midfield

‌



A possibility exists that Arsenal play with more of a flat three in midfield. But where does that leave Odegaard. Or Eberechi Eze, who played centrally last season, or Kai Havertz or eventually Max Dowman?

Arsenal were pipped on penalties by PSG last season as their European Cup dreams were ended in heartbreaking fashion. On that night in Budapest, for all their battling spirit and defensive quality, it was clear that the Gunners had levels to go in the final third to match PSG.

This summer has been about closing that gap. Guimaraes is the type of player who helps them play through the lines. Their pursuit of Vinicius Junior was well publicised.

‌



Arsenal are firmly back among Europe's elite, capping an impressive rise under Arteta's leadership, but if there's one conundrum they're yet to face during the assembly of their stunning squad, it is who to back. In recent years no major player has wanted out, but with so many top class operators now available some will inevitably end up being cannon fodder in the club's grand plan.

Zubimendi may be one of the early lessons.

Sports.title: 'Incredible' Jarrod Bowen move will help West Ham win Championship claims ex-England star
Sports.content:
'Incredible' Jarrod Bowen move will help West Ham win Championship claims ex-England star

Jarrod Bowen’s decision to remain at West Ham despite their relegation is a clear statement of the club’s ambition to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, according to former Hammers striker Dean Ashton.

View 2 Images West Ham United's Jarrod Bowen celebrates scoring against Portsmouth (Image: 2026 CameraSport)

Jarrod Bowen remaining at West Ham in the wake of relegation is a clear sign of the club’s intent to climb straight back into the Premier League this season, according to former Hammers striker Dean Ashton.

‌



West Ham find themselves in the Championship for the first time in 14 years, a dreadful first half to the last campaign ultimately costing them their top-flight status. The club have lost some important players during the summer, such as midfielder Mateus Fernandes and winger Crysencio Summerville, but club captain Bowen will be staying put for their quest for promotion.

‌



Since joining the Hammers from Hull in January 2020, the 29-year-old has become their talisman, scoring 85 goals in 280 appearances, including the winner in the 2023 Conference League final against Fiorentina.

‌



Ahead of their season opener against Burnley, Ashton said: “I think it’s incredible, really, from him and the club, that he has stayed. We’re talking about an England international that may well have hampered those chances of continuing to play for his country with the decision that he’s made.

Ryan Reynolds delivers perfect response to US couple moving from Texas to Wrexham READ MORE :

What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season READ MORE :

“It shows his commitment to the club, but also it shows that West Ham is a big club and that players want to stay and be part of it. He’s got a legacy there and I don’t think he wanted to tarnish that, unless it was a to a real top-level football club, so I think he is going to be their key player.

“If he stays fit, he’ll be the best player in the Championship, in my opinion.”

‌



Bowen was not the only key figure to remain at West Ham this summer, after the club went against some expectations by keeping head coach Nuno Espirito Santo in charge.

After improving the Hammers’ form in the second half of last season, albeit not sufficiently to keep them up, Nuno will be aiming for a second promotion to the Premier League, having achieved the feat with Wolves in the 2017/18 season.

“Hopefully if things start to go well, we’ll start to see a bit more of that passionate side of him.”

‌



Ashton said: “Having a brand that’s recognisable and that people can associate with at these football clubs and connect with them through their football club is really important to supporters.

“Football is fun, that’s why I got into it, so I think the connection between the brand and the EFL is ideal.”

Sports.title: Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his preference clear as Man Utd and Chelsea sounded out
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his preference clear as Man Utd and Chelsea sounded out

Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to Manchester United and Chelsea with the versatile Arsenal teenager making it know to his suitors where he wants to play

View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his midfield ambitions clear (Image: Getty)

Myles Lewis-Skelly has made it clear he wants to play in midfield after Arsenal offered the teenager to rivals Manchester United and Chelsea.

‌



The surprise move comes with the 19-year-old's minutes at the Emirates limited and the signing of Bruno Guimaraes could have further impact that, whilst also closing off the avenue that the academy graduate ultimately wants to pursue.

‌



Lewis-Skelly only agreed a new contract last summer but could end up at another Premier League club, although there is no indication yet over whether United or the Blues will act on Arsenal's offer, as reports football.london.

‌



Michael Carrick's side are looking to sign a midfielder and a left-back before the summer transfer window closes and Lewis-Skelly is capable of playing in both positions - but has made it known that he sees himself as a midfielder.

Chelsea and Man Utd offered Myles Lewis-Skelly as Arsenal open to shock sale despite new deal READ MORE :

Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer READ MORE :

When he first came into the Arsenal team the teenager filled in at left-back, but always had ambitions to move more central. He ultimately started the Champions League final in May alongside Declan Rice in the middle of the park for the Gunners.

Speaking to Arsenal's official website previously Lewis-Skelly has said: "My best position is either a No 6 or No 8. I’m not too sure yet, but I’m just continuing to try my best to master both. Whatever it takes, I’m ready to play in the [No] 6 or [No] 8 role."

‌



Arsenal's signing of Guimaraes means the 19-year-old has the likes of the Brazilian, Rice, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi to compete with for a starting berth. But that could be a problem for him wherever he goes given the midfield depth in Manchester and west London.

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes' signing makes it harder for Myles Lewis-Skelly to push on with his midfield plans (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Chelsea's midfield partnership of Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo is seen as one of the league's best. Fernandez is heavily linked with the exit door, but Xabi Alonso wants to retain him. Even beyond that duo, the Blues have the likes of Romeo Lavia whilst Reece James has also stepped into midfield.

Article continues below

At Old Trafford Michael Carrick has made midfield recruits his priority this summer. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have come through the door with Kobbie Mainoo already in the building. Bruno Fernandes ' role as a 10 means that United only play with two central midfielders, increasing the competition for places.

Sports.title: Max Comley thrilled to get the nod to train first jumps horse for owners Amo Racing
Sports.content:
Max Comley thrilled to get the nod to train first jumps horse for owners Amo Racing

The organisation's leader Kia Joorabchian has kept a half share in twice-raced gelding Diligo, who Comley picked up at the sales for around £40,000 and moved him to his Wiltshire stables

View 2 Images Max Comley (Image: @gallopingpod/X)

High-profile owners Amo Racing will have their first runner over jumps this winter in a link-up with an up-and-coming trainer.

‌



The organisation's leader, businessman and football agent Kia Joorabchian, has kept a half share in Diligo, a three-year-old gelding who made two appearances in maiden events for Joseph O'Brien.

‌



The son of Wootton Bassett was purchased by jockey-turned-trainer Max Comley from the Newmarket July Sales to join his 85-box yard in Wiltshire.

‌



On the back of his best season in 2025-6 with 16 winners, the 28-year-old was asked if Amo Racing could retain an interest in the juvenile hurdling prospect.

Newsboy's tips for all 4 Wednesday meetings including Nap at Salisbury READ MORE :

"I'm a young trainer in the sport and it's great that Kia is supporting us," said 6ft 5in Comley, who quit race-riding after battling with his weight.

"What he has done for racing in a short space of time is fantastic. Last year was our first full season and we are excited to get going with Diligo.

‌



"He has been with us a couple of weeks and we have popped him over some barrels and small jumps. We are pleased that he has a good jumping technique and attitude from what we have seen so far."

Comley grew up near Cheltenham Racecourse, learned to ride and worked for Gold Cup-winning handler Kim Bailey while competing in point-to-points as a teenager.

View 2 Images Kia Joorabchian (Image: Getty Images)

‌



In 2019 he had success with a select string of point-to-pointers and took out a full licence to train under Rules for the 2024-25 campaign.

"Juvenile hurdler Manganese flew the flag for us last season and took us to the Cheltenham Festival," added Comley, soon to plan her next route from a mark of 129.

"It was a great season with 16 winners and we want to build on it now."

Article continues below

Bookmakers Coral are offering odds of 20-1 for Amo Racing to have a winner at the 2027 Cheltenham Festival.

“Amo Racing’s silks are well-known in the Flat racing world, but this move into the jumping fraternity marks a new direction for Kia Joorabchian’s operation," said the firm's David Stevens.

“He may have started in a low-key fashion by taking half of Diligo, but it would be no surprise to see him increase that involvement over the coming months, with a Cheltenham Festival win next March surely on the mind of such an ambitious owner.”

Sports.title: Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow
Sports.content:
Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow

Manchester United are ready to move for Club Brugge left-back Joaquin Seys after seeing their advances for two other targets, including Lewis Hall, knocked back

View 2 Images Joaquin Seys has impressed for Club Brugge with Man Utd now keen

Manchester United are ready to open talks with Club Brugge about a £30million deal for left-back Joaquin Seys after being knocked back by two of their targets.

‌



The Red Devils have added two new faces in midfield but left-back is another area where they are looking to bring in reinforcements. It has proved challenging throughout the summer however with the club onto their third different target.

‌



The Belgian side are in no hurry to sell and have Seys under contract for another three years. They will not ease off their £30m price tag, but it Mirror Football understands United are strongly considering an opening bid.

‌



The 21-year-old is a regular for Club Brugge and forced his way into Belgium‘s World Cup squad, featuring in his country’s quarter-final defeat to winners Spain last month.

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

United did have Newcastle's Lewis Hall on their radar after the ex-Chelsea man had enjoyed the best season of his career to date, but the Magpies are refusing to sell up.

Already this summer Newcastle have lost marquee players in Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes. Hall is one of the leading lights and St James' Park bosses have refused to entertain his departure. United had ultimately been priced out whilst another target, young Spaniard Jorge Salinas, is poised to remain in La Liga.

‌



He reportedly remains fully committed to Racing Santander and "doesn’t want to leave" despite interest from Manchester and Barcelona. His manager Jose Alberto has grown tired with the incessant speculation regarding Salinas’ future during the summer window.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall had been a target for Man Utd (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

The left-back could be available for just €16m (£13.7m) due to a release clause in his contract at Racing, but his boss maintained that he and another of his in-demand team-mates want to remain. "They don’t want him to leave. And they show every day that they don’t either," he said.

‌



"But we know how this world works and there are release clauses. If a team comes along and pays the clause, they cease to be our players."

United currently have Luke Shaw as their first choice left-back, but he has struggled to remain fit throughout his career and, now into his 30s, the club are looking to future proof the position.

Sports.title: Golfer hits staggering 411-yard hole-in-one and is so shocked he can't find the ball
Sports.content:
Golfer hits staggering 411-yard hole-in-one and is so shocked he can't find the ball

An incredible new national record could have been set by an amateur golfer who hit an incredible 411-yard shot, which has estimated odds of six million-to-one

View 4 Images Matt Vigurs hit an incredible 411 yards hole-in-one (Image: Matt Vigurs / SWNS)

A golfer has incredibly set what is thought to be Britain's longest hole-in-one shot, at an incredible 411 yards (376 metres).

‌



Matt Vigurs, from Droitwich in Worcestershire, narrowly missed out on setting a new Guinness World Record when he aced the third hole during a recent match, but he could be in store for a national record. The 32-year-old made the incredible shot during a recent league match at Great Barr Golf Club in Sandwell, near Birmingham.

‌



The golfer hit his driver off the tee but could not find his shot when he reached the green. After a few minutes searching, Matt decided to have a quick look in the hole and saw his ball.

‌



Golf star punished after fish eats his ball during round leaving pundits gobsmacked READ MORE :

View 4 Images The shot was hit at Great Barr Golf Club (Image: Google Maps / SWNS)

Matt said: "It was really surreal. I just froze to start with. The lads ran over and we all belly slammed and high fived. It was a moment I will never forget for sure. It was brilliant. I think we were all shocked. Typically, the ball wouldn't go that far. It is just unheard of to get a hole-in-one really let alone on a par-four."

The golfer revealed that his average drive is around 300 yards but the wind and hard ground helped him stretch out to 411 yards. The incredible shot however was just 36 yards (33 metres) short of all-time record of a 447 yards (408 metres) hole-in-one, set by Robert Mitera in Nebraska, USA.

‌



View 4 Images Matt hit the hole-in-one on his third (Image: Matt Vigurs / SWNS)

Despite this, England Golf - the national governing body for amateur golf - believe Matt could have achieved a national record, but this has not yet been confirmed. It is thought the golfer beat the previous national effort by three yards. Peter Vickerman aced the 408-yard par-four seventh hole at Littlestone Golf Club in Kent, in 2014.

Matt's hole-in-one - also known as an albatross - came in a scratch match at the Walsall golf club, playing with a friend against two others. The four-ball found three balls when they got to the green of the hole, named Twin Oaks - but Matt's was missing.

‌



They searched the bushes, around the fairway and over the back of the green but it was nowhere to be seen. On a whim, Matt, who plays off a handicap of +1, decided to check the hole and says his friends gave him strange looks for even checking.

View 4 Images Matt Vigurs after winning the Worcestershire County Championship (Image: Matt Vigurs / SWNS)

Matt said: "At that point I looked a bit silly, so I thought I might as well check the hole - and there it was, nestled in the bottom. I had to take two or three looks. I couldn't believe it. They didn't believe me till I pulled it out of the hole and we just went mad! It was so weird - I couldn't concentrate for the next hole!"

‌



Matt, who only returned to regular golf in February after eight years abroad, went on to win his match. Droitwich Golf Club as a result sealed promotion by winning the league on the same day.

The odds of getting an albatross - a score of three-under-par - are estimated to be odds of six million-to-one, according to England Golf. However, the odds of a hole-in-one from this distance even likely even slimmer.

Matt, who works as a product and training manager at McLaren, added: "We think it might be the longest which is quite cool actually. I think it might even be the longest in Europe. I have absolutely no chance of ever doing it again. It truly was a once in six-million shot."

Article continues below

The golfer, who started playing the sport aged 11, said he kept the ball and hopes his golf club might help him commemorate the achievement.

James Crampton, championships director at England Golf, said: "We hear of holes-in-one all the time, but a 411-yard one - it's the stuff of golfers' dreams! It sounds like Matt is in the purple patch of his golfing life - and you have to enjoy these moments."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
