World.title: Tinubu seeks global cooperation to tackle emerging security threats
World.content:
Nigeria’s President, Bola Tinubu, has called for stronger national and international cooperation to address emerging security threats confronting Nigeria and the wider world.

Mr Tinubu made the call in Abuja at the ongoing two-day international conference on security, organised by Jama’atu Izalatil Bidiah wa Iqamatis Sunnah (JIBWIS Nigeria) in partnership with the Muslim World League, Saudi Arabia.

The President, who was represented by Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin, said the country was facing “multifaceted” security challenges requiring coordinated and sustainable responses.

According to him, the conference was particularly important given the current security situation and the need for authorities and faith leaders to deliberate on emerging threats to national and digital security systems.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The president said his administration remained committed to ensuring a stable and secure Nigeria while working with other countries and international organisations to promote global security.

“Working within the Committee of Nations, [my government is] collaborating every day to ensure that security remains not only in our country but in the entire globe,” he said.

According to him, the conference was expected to examine emerging trends putting pressure on Nigeria’s national and digital security systems and chart a way forward that would complement the government’s efforts to address the country’s security challenges.

He also called for the preservation of Nigeria’s unity despite differences among its citizens, urging Nigerians to work together to ensure that the country remains united.

Mr Tinubu said participants at the conference would also have an opportunity to exchange experiences and engage in discussions on viable and sustainable options for addressing security challenges.

He commended the Muslim World League for choosing Nigeria as the venue for the conference, describing the decision as significant and assuring that the President was pleased with the event.

He expressed confidence that the deliberations would produce critical and practical outcomes capable of contributing to the government’s security objectives.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the conference comes at a time when religious and ethnic narratives are being exploited by extremists groups in Nigeria and the Sahel region where military juntas are wrestling with rebels and jihadists.

In Nigeria, the security situation continues to deteriorate under President Tinubu with insurgency now spreading to the south where schoolchildren were abducted and their teacher killed by Boko Haram terrorists in May.

READ ALSO: Security forces rescue 16 kidnap victims in Kogi State

Although the government is recording successes at the frontlines, terrorists continue to regroup and increasingly entrench their influence in rural communities where governance is barely present. These ungoverned communities remain key in recruitment drives for terror groups blending religious beliefs with criminality.

Also present at the conference were Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, the national leader of All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, and the Minister of State for Health, Ali Pate.

Others are the Sultan of Sokoto, Muhammad Sa’ad; the Executive Secretary of Nigeria Inter-Religious Council (NIREC), Cornelius Omonokhua; the Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, and his Borno State counterpart, Babagaba Zulum, among others.

World.title: UBA, Mikano Motors ease vehicle ownership with auto financing scheme
World.content:
Africa’s Global Bank, United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc, has partnered Mikano Motors to launch an auto financing scheme, themed: ‘Drive Your Dream Today’, specifically designed to ease the purchase of new vehicles by making them more accessible to Nigerians. The flexible Financing solutions Initiative, requires customers to make an initial payment of just 30 percent while the Bank finances the remaining 70 percent.

Unveiled at the Mikano Motors showroom in Victoria Island, Lagos, the scheme allows eligible customers to repay the financed amount in instalments over a period of 36 months at an interest rate of 23 percent.

The financing is available to a broad range of customers, including individuals who are not on a salaried income, providing entrepreneurs, and other eligible Nigerians with a structured pathway to vehicle ownership.

The process begins with a simple eligibility check. Interested customers can visit their nearest UBA branch or email consumerlending@ ubagroup.com to confirm their eligibility. Once approved, customers can proceed to Mikano Motors to obtain a proforma invoice for their preferred vehicle and continue with the financing process.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Speaking at the launch, UBA’s Group Executive Director, designate, Personal and Business Banking, Chidi Okpala, said the partnership reflects the Bank’s commitment to making everyday aspirations more attainable while promoting a stronger credit culture and advancing financial inclusion.

“Owning a car should not be out of reach for hardworking Nigerians, and this partnership makes it far more achievable,” Okpala said. “A customer puts down 30 percent, we finance the rest, and they pay us back comfortably over a three years period. By removing the single biggest barrier to vehicle ownership where a customer just commits with an upfront cost, we are showing what customer-first banking looks like in practice, which is making their lives easier, by meeting our customers where they are and helping them get where they want to be.”

Also speaking, UBA’s Group Head, Consumer Lending, Frank Okoh, said the scheme was designed to make vehicle financing straightforward and accessible to both salaried and self-employed customers.

“We have kept the entry simple and the terms clear, whether you earn a salary or run your own business,” Okoh said. “A short eligibility check at any branch or by email is all it takes to begin, and our team guides the customer through every step to the moment they collect their keys.”

For Mikano Motors, the partnership provides an opportunity to extend its vehicle ownership proposition to a wider pool of Nigerians

The company’s General Manager, Tarek Mostafa, said the collaboration aligns with Mikano Motors’ vision of providing customers with a high-end ownership experience supported by reliable after-sales services.

“Mikano Motors was established to give Nigerians a high-end ownership experience, from the showroom to years down the road,” Mostafa said. “The backbone of any automotive business is not just the sale, but the after-sales service that follows. Every vehicle we sell is backed by genuine spare parts, reliable maintenance and quality service available anywhere in the country. Wherever you are we would come meet you at no extra cost”

“Partnering with UBA lets more customers enjoy that experience, and we are proud to build lasting relationships alongside a bank that shares our commitment to service,” he added.

Established in 2018 under Mikano International, Mikano Motors builds on more than 35 years of the group’s presence in Nigeria. The company offers a diversified portfolio of vehicles supported by nationwide sales and after-sales services.

The partnership further strengthens UBA’s consumer lending proposition, providing customers with structured financing solutions designed around accessibility, affordability and convenience. Through partnerships such as this, the Bank continues to expand access to credit while helping customers meet significant personal and lifestyle needs with ease.

United Bank for Africa is one of the largest employers in the financial sector on the African continent, with 25,000 employees group-wide and serving over 45 million customers globally. Operating in twenty African countries, the United Kingdom, the United States of America, France and the United Arab Emirates, UBA provides retail, commercial and institutional banking services, leading financial inclusion and implementing cutting-edge technology.

World.title: Passengers stranded as airlines suspend, reschedule flights amid aviation unions’ strike
World.content:
Passengers remained stranded at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on Tuesday afternoon as aviation unions continued their industrial action, disrupting flight operations and forcing some airlines to suspend or reschedule services.

The disruption also affected operations at the Lagos airport, where Air Peace earlier reported that union members barricaded access to its departure terminals.

Air Peace, Enugu Air and United Nigeria Airlines announced disruptions to their operations, with the airlines either suspending or rescheduling flights because of restricted access to airport terminals.

The industrial action is linked to grievances by aviation unions over workers’ freedom to unionise and the alleged non-remittance of the five per cent Ticket Sales Charge (TSC) collected from passengers.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Flight disruption

Air Peace earlier in its statement said the entrances to its departure terminals at the Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal 1, including the Alpha and Zulu terminals, and Terminal 2 in Lagos, as well as the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport terminal in Abuja, had been barricaded.

The airline added that the blockade restricted access to the terminals and prevented scheduled flights from departing Lagos and Abuja.

Air Peace apologised to affected and stranded passengers and said those scheduled to travel later in the day were being contacted with updates as the situation developed.

Enugu Air also announced the temporary suspension of operations at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, after union workers allegedly denied its staff access to the terminal.

The airline said the disruption could result in the rescheduling of some flights while it adjusted its network.

“Please be informed that due to an ongoing industrial action at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, where union workers are denying staff access into the airport terminal, operations at the airport have been temporarily suspended,” the airline said in a notice.

“Consequently, some of Enugu Air flights may experience rescheduling until further notice, as we work to adjust our network,” it added.

The airline apologised to affected passengers and advised them to check their email, SMS and official social media platforms for updates before proceeding to the airport.

It also advised passengers requiring assistance with rebooking or other enquiries to contact its customer service team.

United Nigeria Airlines similarly announced a temporary suspension of its flight operations because of the industrial action.

The airline said it took the decision to protect the safety of its passengers and crew and would keep affected passengers informed of revised schedules.

It apologised for the inconvenience and advised affected passengers to contact its customer care team for assistance.

The airlines said they would resume normal operations once normalcy returned at the affected airports.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the NCAA Director-General, Chris Najomo, urged the aviation unions to suspend their industrial action pending the return of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, who the regulator said was working to resolve the dispute.

READ ALSO: Nigerian airlines may go extinct within 30 days Onyema

The regulator appealed to all parties to embrace dialogue and cooperation, expressing confidence that the matter would be resolved and normal flight operations restored. It also assured passengers that flight safety had not been compromised and that the NCAA continued to discharge its statutory safety oversight responsibilities.

The disruption has left passengers facing uncertainty over their travel plans, with those at Abuja airport still waiting as airlines adjust their schedules in response to the industrial action.

The latest developments have brought the consequences of the dispute directly to passengers, with airlines unable to operate some scheduled flights because of restricted access to airport terminals.

Passengers travelling through affected airports have consequently been advised to monitor updates from their airlines before heading to the airport.

World.title: 5 phones made in China that can rival the Samsung Galaxy S26
World.content:
The global phones market is becoming increasingly competitive, with manufacturers in China producing flagship devices that combine powerful processors, advanced cameras, fast charging and premium designs.

Samsung’s Galaxy S26 series remains one of the major names in the premium smartphone segment, but several Chinese brands are offering devices that can compete strongly in areas such as photography, performance, battery technology and artificial intelligence.

For consumers looking beyond Samsung, here are five Chinese smartphones that can rival the Galaxy S26.

1. Xiaomi 17 Ultra

Xiaomi’s flagship Ultra series has established itself as a serious competitor in the premium smartphone market, particularly in mobile photography.

The Xiaomi 17 Ultra is aimed at users who prioritise camera performance, with the company continuing its partnership with Leica to improve imaging capabilities.

Beyond photography, the phone combines flagship-level processing power with a premium display and high-end hardware, making it one of the Chinese smartphones capable of going head-to-head with Samsung’s Galaxy S26.

2. Huawei Pura 80 Ultra

Huawei’s Pura series has become particularly known for its focus on smartphone photography, and the Pura 80 Ultra continues that approach.

The device is designed around advanced camera technology, making it an attractive option for consumers who place photography high on their list when choosing a premium phone.

Huawei has also continued developing its own ecosystem and software experience, giving the Pura 80 Ultra a distinct position among high-end Chinese smartphones.

3. Vivo X300 Pro

Vivo has built a strong reputation for smartphone photography and premium hardware through its X series.

The Vivo X300 Pro targets the flagship segment with a powerful processor, an advanced camera system and a high-quality display.

Its emphasis on photography, combined with performance and battery capabilities, makes it one of the Chinese phones that can compete with Samsung’s Galaxy S26 in the premium market.

4. Oppo Find X9 Pro

Oppo’s Find X series is another major challenger to Samsung in the high-end smartphone segment.

The Find X9 Pro combines a premium design with flagship performance, advanced cameras and fast charging technology.

Oppo has increasingly focused on computational photography and artificial intelligence, areas that have become central to competition among premium smartphone manufacturers.

Its combination of hardware and software features makes the Find X9 Pro a strong alternative for buyers considering a Galaxy S26.

5. Honor Magic V6

Honor is taking a slightly different approach with the Magic V6 by competing in the foldable smartphone segment.

Rather than following the conventional flagship design, the Magic V6 offers a foldable form factor while maintaining high-end specifications.

Its slim design, large flexible display and flagship hardware put it in competition with Samsung’s foldable devices while also demonstrating how quickly Chinese manufacturers are advancing in the premium smartphone market.

World.title: Girl suffers deformed finger after family burns her over N500
World.content:
Young black girl counts to 5 on her fingers, slow motion, shallow depth of field

By Mary Agbabiaka

A 12-year-old girl has suffered a severe burn and permanent deformity to her index finger after a family she was staying with allegedly punished her by burning the finger over an accusation that she stole N500.

The incident occurred months ago when the girl was taken to an emergency paediatric unit by a middle-aged female police officer, about 10 days after she sustained the burn.

According to the doctor, Tortiv Samuel Msev, who attended to her, the girl’s parents lived in a village and had sent her to stay with another family in town.

The doctor said the family accused the girl of stealing N500 and subjected her to what he described as a “hellfire punishment,” burning her index finger until it became deformed.

He said the girl was also forced to continue doing household chores without proper wound care, even as the injury worsened.

“No pain compares that of a burn,” the doctor wrote, adding that it took the intervention of neighbours to rescue the girl and alert the police.

The account took another turn when one of the family members reportedly confessed to the police that they had taken the money, proving that the child had been wrongly accused.

Reflecting on the incident, the doctor said the experience had remained with him and made him reflect on the responsibilities of parents and other adults entrusted with the care of children.

“That moment stayed with me”.

“As parents, praying for longevity is beyond our cravings for the beautiful things of this world, but that we may be there and strong enough to care for our children”.

The doctor expressed concern that the girl would have to live with the physical and emotional consequences of the abuse.

“The little girl will grow up with a deformed finger constantly reminding her of how below the bare minimum adults around her fell,” he wrote.

World.title: Why Lagos waste crisis is now worse – Dep. Gov Hamzat
World.content:
Lagos State Deputy Governor, Obafemi Hamzat, has attributed the worsening waste situation in the state to a combination of increased waste generation, a shortage of functional waste collection trucks and challenges facing private sector operators.

Hamzat said the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), which is responsible for waste management in the state, had been tasked with handling a volume of refuse that was significantly higher than originally anticipated.

Speaking on Nigerian Info 99.3fm, the Deputy Governor said the government initially estimated that Lagos generated about 13,000 tonnes of waste daily but later discovered that the actual figure was closer to 17,000 tonnes.

“Well, so, you know, you know, it’s easy for me to just throw the agency under the bus, but I won’t do that. That’s the agency that’s responsible, that we all know, LAWMA. But it’s, so we’ve asked them to do a job, the scale of which we did not predict,” Hamzat said.

“And that scale is really unprecedented in this part of the world. So we thought that we are generating 13 tonnes on a daily basis. It turns out we are generating about 17,000.”

According to the Deputy Governor, the discrepancy in waste generation figures has made it difficult for the state government to accurately plan and manage waste collection across Lagos.

“No, no, no. So, it’s figures. So that’s why we said, you know, if you go around every part of Africa, if you go to Accra, Lagos, Lome, Freetown, what you see is disorganisation,” he said.

“As a people, the first thing we need to do is we need to organise ourselves. So how do you plan for something you can’t measure? How? So people sleep on the street, this and that. So if you don’t, what you can’t measure, it’s difficult to plan and manage it.”

Hamzat noted that waste is also generated by people living and carrying out activities on the streets, making it more difficult for authorities to accurately determine the volume of refuse produced.

“Do you understand? So the people that sleep on the street, that man or those men or young boys that went and scraped the street, they generate refuse. How do we plan for that? How do we know?” he asked.

The Deputy Governor also identified rising operational costs and a shortage of functional waste collection trucks among the factors affecting refuse collection.

He said Lagos has about 420 Private Sector Participants (PSPs) involved in waste collection, with each operator expected under its agreement with the government to have at least two trucks.

“So unfortunately, because of also the war that Iran, whatever, all this world that’s happened, our trucks. So we have about 420 or so PSPs,” Hamzat said.

“So these are private sector people that carry the refuse. Each of them by agreement must have two trucks before you can do. So we are, we are expected about over 800 trucks.”

However, he said many of the operators no longer have the required number of trucks because some vehicles have become unusable or businesses have shut down.

“The reality is that a lot of them don’t have two anymore. Either it has shut down. They wanted to, they came to us to say, well, cost of diesel has gone up. We want to increase the tariff,” he said.

Hamzat said the state government rejected the proposed tariff increase but agreed to provide additional support to the operators.

“And finally we said, no, don’t increase the tariff. Let the state pay,” he said.

“But we negotiated. So let’s say they wanted to go by X. We said, no, X minus Y. Y is a positive integer to say instead of 10 Naira, let it be, you know, four, five, and then we pay it to them. So that was the first challenge.”

Hamzat said the state government subsequently discovered that a significant number of the existing waste collection trucks were no longer fit for use, prompting it to order new vehicles.

“The second challenge is that we realise that a lot of the trucks are no longer usable. So we order trucks,” he said.

According to him, Lagos has 57 local government and local council development areas, with two trucks planned for each, amounting to 114 vehicles. The state government also ordered another 100 trucks.

“We were supposed to get delivery in July. Unfortunately, they now said it’s going to be September,” Hamzat said.

The delay, he explained, was one of the reasons he was reluctant to blame LAWMA entirely for the current waste situation.

“So when I said I will not throw LAWMA under the bus, it’s because of something like that. It’s not technically their fault. Maybe we should have ordered earlier. Maybe. I mean, we must take responsibility,” the Deputy Governor said.

Vanguard News

World.title: Osun election: SERAP urges INEC to act over rising political violence
World.content:
The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to urgently identify, document and publicly report growing incidents of political violence, threats and intimidation ahead of Saturday’s governorship election in Osun State.

SERAP also called on INEC to take preventive measures to protect voters and candidates and ensure that the election is conducted in a peaceful and secure atmosphere.

In a statement, the organisation urged the electoral commission to promptly refer credible allegations of electoral violence and related offences to the Nigeria Police Force and other appropriate law enforcement and security agencies for thorough, impartial, independent and transparent investigation and prosecution.

SERAP said victims of political violence and their families must be provided access to justice and effective remedies.

The organisation said there had been reports of 56 politically related violent incidents and 14 fatalities in Osun over the past 12 months, with 36 incidents recorded in May and June alone.

According to SERAP, reported incidents include shootings, killings, physical attacks, intimidation, destruction of property and harassment.

It said INEC had recognised political violence in Osun as a serious electoral-security concern and urged the commission to strengthen threat assessment, monitoring and coordination with law enforcement and security agencies.

SERAP further urged INEC to document and preserve credible evidence of serious, widespread or systematic political violence in the state and, where conduct may amount to crimes within the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court, bring the evidence to the attention of appropriate national and international accountability mechanisms, including the ICC Prosecutor.

The organisation cited Section 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which prohibits threats of force or violence during political campaigns.

It also cited Section 14(2)(c) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides for the participation of the people in their government, as well as Sections 39 and 40, which protect freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association. Section 42 guarantees equality and non-discrimination.

“No election should be conducted in an atmosphere of fear,” SERAP said, stressing that Nigerians have the right to vote for candidates of their choice.

The organisation urged INEC to ensure that security arrangements protect voters, candidates, journalists, observers and civil society organisations without political discrimination.

SERAP called on the commission to act immediately to protect the integrity of the Osun election and safeguard every voter’s right to participate freely and safely without fear, intimidation or coercion.

World.title: 2027 Polls: NHRC asks FG to arrest, prosecute Sheikh Jingir for hate speech
World.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), on Tuesday, urged the Federal Government to immediately arrest and prosecute Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Jingir, for hate speech and incitement.

The Commission, in a statement signed by its Executive Secretary, Chief Tony Ojukwu, SAN, said it condemned in strong terms “the hateful and inciting remarks” it said were made by the cleric in a viral video on Sunday.

The NHRC said it watched with grave concern as the cleric openly canvassed for religiously exclusive politics ahead of the general elections and used derogatory language referring to “infidels” while urging supporters to obtain voter cards to “show their limit.”

The rights body described the statements as a direct attack on the principles of equality, non-discrimination, and peaceful coexistence guaranteed under the 1999 Constitution, as amended, and Nigeria’s international human rights obligations.

“The Commission finds these remarks to be hate speech and incitement to religious hatred and potential violence. At a time when we are preparing for another general election, such utterances are reckless and dangerous.

“They serve no purpose other than to divide Nigerians along religious lines and set citizens against one another.

“We cannot afford to look away. If we fail to speak and act now, we embolden both Christian and Muslim clerics and other influential persons to make worse statements in the coming months. That path leads only to crisis,” the Commission stated.

Consequently, it called on the Inspector General of Police, the Director General of the Department of State Services, and other relevant authorities to immediately arrest and prosecute Sheikh Jingir for hate speech and incitement.

The Commission implored religious leaders, traditional rulers, and politicians to refrain from divisive rhetoric, even as it urged Nigerians to reject identity politics and to hold leaders accountable based on competence, service delivery, and respect for human rights.

“Prosecution must proceed irrespective of status or political affiliation in order to serve as a deterrent to others who may seek to exploit religion for political gain during this election period.

“The Commission will continue to monitor compliance and will engage with security agencies, INEC, and civil society to ensure that the 2027 elections are free from hate and violence,” the statement further read.

World.title: Photos: Customs intercept explosives, expired noodles, narcotics at Seme Border
World.content:
Comptroller Abdullahi Kaila with other officers of the Seme Border Command displaying some of the seized contrabands earlier today.

By Godwin Oritse

The Seme Border Command of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) on Tuesday dealt a major blow to smuggling and cross-border criminal activities with the interception of explosive materials, expired noodles, Savita Cannabis and other prohibited items.

Disclosing this to stakeholders at the border town, Comptroller of the command Controller Abdullahi Kaila said that intelligence and sustained surveillance, officers subjected the consignment to thorough examination and uncovered 1,306 sacks of expired and waste noodles, each weighing 50 kilograms.

Kaila also described the discovery as worrisome, noting that the expired noodles could have posed serious health risks to unsuspecting Nigerians who might have purchased and consumed them.

He said:”Acting on intelligence and sustained surveillance, our officers subjected the consignment to thorough examination and uncovered 1,306 sacks of expired and waste noodles, each weighing 50 kilograms.

“What was discovered was deeply disturbing because many of the products had already deteriorated and were visibly decomposing. Intelligence further revealed that the intention was to repackage, relabel and introduce these products into Nigerian markets for unsuspecting consumers.

“Had this shipment succeeded, countless families would have been exposed to serious health hazards ranging from food poisoning and gastrointestinal diseases to other life-threatening medical complications.

“By intercepting these products, the Nigeria Customs Service has once again demonstrated that border security is also a form of public health protection. Every child, every family and every Nigerian has been protected from what could have become a silent public health disaster.

“Furthermore, in separate enforcement operations conducted across different flashpoints within our area of responsibility, the Command also intercepted 1,268 bags of foreign parboiled rice, each weighing 50 kilograms, smuggled through illegal routes.

“Beyond denying government legitimate revenue, such illicit importation undermines the Federal Government’s agricultural policies, discourages local rice production and threatens the livelihoods of Nigerian farmers.

Seized

“The fight against illicit drugs remains one of the Service’s critical contributions to national security and public safety. Pursuant to this, the Command intercepted the following shipments:

373 parcels of Cannabis Sativa, 90 packs of Tramaking 250mg, 69 packs of Royal Tapentadol 250mg and 310,000 sticks of Time/Yes cigarettes.

“These are not ordinary commodities, they are dangerous products capable of destroying lives, fueling criminality, encouraging substance abuse and undermining the future of our young people.

“The illicit drugs intercepted are often linked to cultism, armed robbery, violent crimes and other social vices, while smuggled cigarettes evade health regulations, avoid payment of statutory duties and expose consumers to products outside approved quality standards.

“Through these interceptions, the Seme Area Command has disrupted criminal supply chains and prevented these dangerous products from reaching our communities.

“Our officers intercepted 3,300 cartridges of explosive materials being illegally conveyed through the border corridor. Explosives of this nature have devastating consequences when they fall into the hands of criminal elements. They have the potential to facilitate terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other violent crimes capable of threatening national peace and security.

“The successful interception of these explosives demonstrates the vigilance, professionalism and intelligence-driven operations of our officers, working in close collaboration with sister security agencies.

“Considering the sensitive nature of the seizure, the explosive materials have already been handed over to the Nigeria Police Force Explosive Ordnance Disposal Unit for safe custody and further investigation.

“I must emphasize that our renewed resolve to fight smuggling and cross-border crimes using intelligence is paying off and continues to disrupt the activities of those bent on sabotaging our economy.

“As part of its anti-smuggling efforts, the Command intercepted one used speedboat, one used Water Bike, one used Toyota Land Cruiser (2017 Model), one used Toyota RAV4 (2016 Model) and one used Nissan Versa (2010 Model) with Duty Paid Value ₦365,1Million.

“While enforcement remains highly visible, it represents only one dimension of our statutory responsibilities. The second is facilitating legitimate trade while generating revenue for national development.

“In 2025, the Seme Area Command’s achievement reflected improved compliance, enhanced stakeholder engagement, and strengthened operational efficiency as our revenue performance in 2026 has been even more remarkable, between January and July 2026.

“The Command generated ₦19,8Billion. as against ₦15,9Billion generated in 2025. This means that within only seven months, the Command has surpassed its entire twelve-month revenue collection for 2025 by ₦3,899,022,112.49, representing a 24.45 per cent increase.”

World.title: Oyo abduction: Judicial panel seeks public evidence on 46 victims’ 56-day ordeal
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

The Judicial Commission of Inquiry set up by the Oyo State Government to unravel the circumstances surrounding the abduction of 46 pupils and teachers in Oriire Local Government Area has invited members of the public to submit evidence that could assist its investigation.

The government, in a statement issued on Tuesday, said the commission was seeking relevant information on the circumstances surrounding the abduction of pupils, students and teachers from the Esinele and Yawota communities, as well as the security response before, during and after the attack.

“The Judicial Commission of Inquiry into the Oriire abduction is calling for public memoranda,” the government stated.

It gave Friday, August 14, 2026, as the deadline for the submission of memoranda, urging individuals and organisations with useful information about the incident to come forward and assist the panel in establishing the facts surrounding one of the state’s most serious security incidents in recent times.

According to the government, submissions to the commission should contain the full name and contact details of the contributor, alongside any supporting documents considered relevant to the information being provided.

The government said memoranda could be submitted physically at the Conference Room, Office of the Head of Service, State Secretariat, Agodi, Ibadan.

It also provided an electronic channel for submissions through [email protected], urging members of the public with relevant information to ensure that their memoranda reached the commission before the August 14 deadline.

The commission’s terms of reference include receiving information concerning the abduction of pupils, students and teachers from communities including Esinele and Yawota and examining the security response to the incident before, during and after the attack.

The development came months after armed men attacked three schools in Oriire Local Government Area on May 15, 2026, abducting dozens of pupils and teachers.

The affected schools were Community High School, Ahoro-Esinele; Baptist Nursery and Primary School, Yawota; and L.A. Primary School.

A total of 39 students and seven teachers were taken captive during the attack and remained in the custody of their abductors for 56 days before their eventual rescue in July.

The release of the victims was announced by the Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, who said security agencies had rescued them without making any concession to the abductors.

The prolonged captivity generated widespread concern across Oyo State and beyond, while security agencies subsequently intensified operations to secure the victims and bring the ordeal to an end.

Following the rescue, Governor Seyi Makinde called for an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding the abduction, describing the incident as grave enough to warrant scrutiny beyond the existing domestic institutions.

The latest move by the state government therefore marked a formal effort to obtain first-hand accounts, documentary evidence and other relevant information that could help the commission reconstruct what happened before, during and after the attack.

Beyond determining the circumstances that led to the abduction, the inquiry is also expected to examine the adequacy and effectiveness of the security response, including what actions were taken before the attack, the response during the incident and the measures adopted afterwards.

The government urged members of the public who witnessed events connected with the abduction or possess relevant information or documentation to make their contributions to the commission within the stipulated period.

It said such submissions could assist the judicial panel in its investigation and help establish a clearer account of the incident.

“The Oyo State Government remains committed to the safety of every community,” the statement added.

The public invitation for memoranda came against the backdrop of continuing concerns over the security of schools and communities in parts of the state, particularly following the scale and duration of the Oriire incident.

The government consequently urged anyone with relevant information to take advantage of the opportunity to submit evidence before the August 14 deadline, as the commission continues its investigation into the abduction that kept 46 pupils and teachers in captivity for nearly two months.

World.title: FG backs West Africa petrol pricing benchmark
World.content:
Heineken Lokpobiri

— S&P Global urges market participation

By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

The Federal Government has backed the establishment of a regional petrol pricing benchmark for West Africa, saying the initiative would strengthen energy security, deepen cross-border trade and enable the region to determine the value of its refined petroleum products.

The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Heineken Lokpobiri, stated this yesterday at the 2026 West Africa Refined Fuel Market, WAFRFM, Conference in Abuja, where regulators, refiners, traders, investors and other industry stakeholders discussed the development of a regional petroleum pricing and trading hub.

Lokpobiri said Nigeria’s decision to deregulate the downstream petroleum sector was aimed at unlocking investment and allowing market forces to play a greater role in determining petroleum prices.

He said the country’s expanding refining capacity and strategic position in Africa placed Nigeria in a strong position to support the emergence of a more integrated West African petroleum market.

The minister, however, stressed that Nigeria could not achieve the objective alone, urging stronger cooperation among West African countries and greater alignment of regulatory frameworks.

“If we are successful in Nigeria, we haven’t achieved our objective. We want Ghana to succeed,” he said.

According to him, the regional market should enable countries to maximise their respective advantages, facilitate investment and reduce dependence on pricing structures determined outside Africa.

Lokpobiri said Nigeria was committed to supporting the initiative and attracting investment into refining and the broader downstream petroleum value chain.

From roadmap to execution

Chief Executive of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, Rabiu Umar, said the 2026 conference marked a transition from developing a roadmap to implementing it.

He said the inaugural conference in 2025 laid the foundation for a West African refined-products reference market, with emphasis on refining capacity, logistics, storage, infrastructure, regulatory cooperation, market data and access to capital.

Umar said progress had been recorded a year later, particularly through the West Africa Regulators Forum and collaboration with S&P Global Commodity Insights to bring market reporting and benchmark expertise closer to regional transactions and physical product flows.

He cautioned, however, that a benchmark could not exist in isolation.

“A reference price is not by itself a trading hub. A conference is not a market,” Umar said, stressing that credible price discovery required physical infrastructure, commercial liquidity, reliable market information and operational efficiency.

He said West Africa must develop the infrastructure required to move petroleum products efficiently from refineries to storage facilities, terminals and ports, and ultimately across borders to demand centres.

According to him, the infrastructure requirements include refineries, pipelines, storage terminals, jetties, ports, roads, rail networks, marine logistics, strategic reserves and digital trading platforms.

Umar described the region’s infrastructure deficit as an opportunity for investors, identifying pipelines, product transportation systems, storage facilities, marine terminals, refinery expansion and optimisation, road and rail logistics, gas infrastructure, digital commodity exchanges and trading platforms as potential areas for investment.

He said capital would only flow into projects that were bankable, supported by predictable regulations and capable of delivering sustainable returns.

“For investors, predictability matters. For operators, efficiency matters. For consumers, affordability and reliability matter. For regulators, safety, integrity, competition and compliance matter,” he said.

The NMDPRA chief also called for greater operational efficiency, particularly at ports and terminals, saying delays, demurrage, transportation costs and inefficient infrastructure could undermine the competitiveness of the regional market.

He identified five priorities for the next phase of the initiative: deepening physical market liquidity, financing strategic infrastructure, harmonising regulations and product standards, institutionalising market transparency and building a complete trading ecosystem.

Such an ecosystem, he said, must include refiners, traders, terminal operators, ship owners, marketers, banks, insurers, commodity exchanges, data providers and regulators.

Also speaking, the Special Adviser to the President on Energy, Olu Verheijen, said West Africa was not short of energy resources or demand but was constrained by fragmented markets and inadequate infrastructure.

She said Nigeria’s growing refining capacity and declining dependence on imported petrol had created an opportunity for the country to serve as an anchor for a more integrated regional petroleum market.

“Refining capacity alone, as big as ours is, does not create energy security,” she said.

Verheijen said refined products must be financed, stored, transported and distributed efficiently before they could deliver their full economic value.

She called for investment in pipelines, ports, storage facilities, coastal vessels, trucking networks and trading platforms, as well as common product standards and stronger cooperation among regional regulators.

She said the ambition should be for petroleum products refined in West Africa to be traded and priced within the region instead of leaving the continent before their value is determined.

On her part, the Chief Executive of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, NUPRC, Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, said developments across Nigeria’s oil and gas value chain had created an opportunity to complete the integration of West Africa’s petroleum market.

She cited rising refining capacity, improved gas supply and increased crude oil production as major developments that could support the regional initiative.

Eyesan said West African countries must move away from operating in isolated national markets.

“The West African market must be integrated. We can no longer afford to operate in silos,” she said.

She called for integrated regulatory systems and infrastructure capable of connecting producers, refiners, traders and consumers across the sub-region.

S&P Global urges market participation

In her remarks, Vera Blei, Head of Platts, S&P Global Energy, said the company had expanded its regional refined-product price assessments and increased the frequency of market updates in response to heightened market volatility.

She said S&P Global was also developing additional data and reporting mechanisms for West Africa to improve transparency and support regional price discovery.

Blei disclosed that the pricing benchmark was being developed in naira and other local currencies in the West African sub-region, adding that the company had opened an office in Abuja to facilitate its operations.

She, however, stressed that while regulators and price-reporting agencies could provide the foundations, market participants would ultimately have to create a liquid and credible benchmark through actual transactions.

She urged refiners, traders and other market participants to use and transact against emerging regional benchmarks if they wanted them to become established references.

World.title: Health Workers Issue Katsina 21-day Ultimatum to Meet Demands
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The Assembly of Health Care Professionals in Katsina State has threatened to embark on industrial action if the state government fails to address its welfare and professional demands within 21 days.

Addressing journalists in Katsina Tuesday on behalf of the Assembly, the state Chairman of the Association of Hospital and Administrative Pharmacists of Nigeria, Comrade Ibrahim Balange, said the members of the union would embark on strike after the expiration of the ultimatum.

He explained that the ultimatum, which took effect on August 11, 2026, was issued after several engagements, meetings and representations to the state government failed to produce significant progress on the workers’ demands.

He said the health professionals were demanding the immediate implementation of 100 per cent Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) as applicable in Federal Government-owned health institutions.

He noted that the health workers are also demanding the skipping of CONHESS 10, as contained in previous government circulars and correspondence submitted to relevant committees in the state.

Balange said the assembly was further demanding an upward review of the hazard allowance to 100 per cent, in line with what is obtainable in federal health institutions.

Other demands, he said, included upward review of call duty, shift, clinical and non-clinical, rural and specialist allowances, as well as an increase in nurses’ uniform allowance to N80,000, as applicable in federal health institutions.

He said the demands were not aimed at undermining the government but were necessary to improve the welfare and motivation of health workers and ultimately strengthen healthcare delivery in Katsina State.

Balange expressed concern that the prolonged delay in resolving the issues was affecting the morale and productivity of healthcare professionals whom he said, despite the challenges, remained committed to serving residents of the state.

He warned that failure by the government to meet the demands within the 21-day ultimatum would leave the health professionals with no option but to down tools.

He, however, appealed to the state government to use the period of the ultimatum to resolve the issues and avert a disruption of healthcare services across the state.

He said the Assembly remained hopeful that Governor Dikko Umaru Radda’s administration would respond positively to the demands in the interest of healthcare workers and the people of the state.

Balange revealed that the Assembly, comprising the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria, National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives, Association of Hospital and Administrative Pharmacists of Nigeria and Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists of Nigeria, had been patient with the government over the issues.

World.title: The Man Between Market and the State
World.content:
Kehinde Sowole writes on how Temi Popoola and NGX Group are turning economic reform into capital formation

Every era of economic reform produces two kinds of figures. There are the reformers themselves, the presidents, ministers and governors who take the political risk of change. And there are the interlocutors: the institutional leaders who translate reform into confidence, policy into capital, and government ambition into market reality. Nigeria’s current reform era has no shortage of the first kind. What has become increasingly evident is the emergence of the second, and few embody that role more convincingly today like Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Nigerian Exchange Group.

Last week’s engagement between the NGX Group Board and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the State House was, on its surface, a courtesy visit. Read properly, it was something rarer: a working session between a government pursuing economic transformation and a capital market leadership that has positioned the market as an increasingly indispensable instrument for delivering that transformation. The numbers presented to the president told one story; market capitalisation rising from under N30 trillion in 2023 to about N160 trillion today, while the All-Share Index climbed from roughly 52,000 to over 244,000 points. The rally reflects the positive response of investors to recent macroeconomic reforms, while also building on decades of institutional development by market operators, listed companies, regulators and investors. But the more consequential story came afterwards was the president’s affirmation that NNPC Limited will be reformed and listed on the capital market, alongside his endorsement of the market’s role in financing Nigeria’s ambition of becoming a one-trillion-dollar economy.

That a sitting Nigerian president now speaks of the stock exchange as an instrument of national economic strategy, in the same breath as fiscal and monetary policy did not happen by accident. It reflects years of deliberate work by institutions across Nigeria’s capital market ecosystem to reposition the market from a spectator of economic policy to an active participant in national development. Throughout that evolution, Popoola has emerged as one of its most influential advocates and architects, helping to articulate a vision of the capital market not merely as a trading venue, but as infrastructure for national growth.

Consider the record. When the banking sector recapitalisation programme was announced, sceptics predicted overwhelming dependence on foreign capital. Instead, roughly three-quarters of the funds were mobilised domestically, supported by NGX Invest, a market infrastructure that NGX Group and the wider ecosystem had modernised for exactly such moments. When Nigeria migrated to T+1 settlement this June, placing it among the more efficient emerging markets in post-trade settlement, it reflected years of coordinated technical work involving exchanges, regulators, clearing institutions and market participants. When international index providers questioned aspects of the market’s structure, NGX Group’s leadership responded with evidence rather than rhetoric. And when Dangote Petroleum Refinery signalled its intention to list, it reinforced a proposition Popoola has consistently advanced: Nigeria’s largest enterprises should increasingly seek long-term capital from Nigerian markets, allowing more Nigerians to participate in the country’s economic growth.

What distinguishes Popoola’s leadership is its refusal of the adversarial posture that has often characterised relations between African markets and African governments. Exchange leaders have traditionally oscillated between supplication and criticism, either asking governments for concessions or lamenting policy shortcomings. Popoola has helped shape a different approach: partnership not with any particular administration, but with credible economic reform itself. The four priorities presented at the State House; the privatisation and listing of viable government assets, dual listings by leading Nigerian companies, clarity around capital gains tax treatment, and greater use of capital markets to finance infrastructure, were less a list of requests than a proposed division of labour. Government provides policy clarity, assets and reform momentum; the capital market provides capital formation, price discovery, transparency and broad-based ownership.

The NNPC commitment is the first major test of that division of labour, and it is difficult to overstate what it could represent. A listed NNPC would mean audited accounts where opacity has often prevailed, market discipline where political discretion has historically dominated, and perhaps most significantly, an opportunity for millions of Nigerians, directly and through their pension funds to own a stake in one of the country’s most strategic commercial enterprises. It is privatisation not as transfer to a connected few, but as broader public participation. If executed successfully, it could become one of the defining institutional reforms of this era. NGX would provide the platform, while years of investment in settlement systems, market infrastructure, retail participation and institutional capacity would help explain why the market is increasingly prepared for transactions of such scale.

None of this eliminates the difficult questions. Nigeria’s cost-of-living pressures remain real, and rising equity indices do not immediately reduce household expenses, a reality acknowledged by both Popoola and Central Bank Governor Yemi Cardoso. The trillion-dollar economy remains an aspiration requiring sustained growth well beyond recent performance. And the distance between a presidential commitment and a completed listing is one on which many reform programmes have faltered. Yet this is precisely why institutional leadership matters. Commitments become transactions only when there are credible institutions capable of executing them and leaders trusted by policymakers, domestic investors and international capital alike. That institutional credibility built patiently over time may prove to be one of the most valuable assets the Nigerian capital market possesses.

The history of successful reforming economies demonstrates that governments alone do not build vibrant capital markets, nor do capital markets reform governments in isolation. Progress emerges through productive collaboration between credible public policy and strong market institutions. That collaboration must outlast any administration because markets ultimately create wealth through rules, not rulers. The strongest testament to NGX Group’s growing institutional maturity is that its case for deeper capital markets would remain the same regardless of who occupies political office. In Nigeria’s reform moment, Popoola has become one of the principal figures helping to occupy that critical space between policy and capital. The president has now said publicly what many market participants have long believed: if the stock market is doing well, Nigeria’s economy is moving in the right direction. The task now is to ensure that confidence continues to translate into investment, reform into opportunity, and market performance into lasting national prosperity.

· Sowole, a financial expert, is based in Lagos

World.title: UBEC Urges States to Fully Utilise Basic Education Funds
World.content:
* Delta reports 90% implementation of 2025 action plan

Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) has called on states to ensure full utilisation of available funds and prompt implementation of approved programmes to improve basic education delivery across Nigeria.

The call was made during a courtesy visit to the Delta State Government, represented by Deputy Governor, Monday Onyeme, in Asaba, as part of the 30th quarterly meeting of UBEC management with executive chairmen of State Universal Basic Education Boards (SUBEBs).

The meeting, themed, ‘Repositioning Basic Education in Nigeria to Optimise Investment and Impact,’ focused on how investments and innovations can translate into better classrooms and learning outcomes.

UBEC commended Delta State for accessing its UBE matching grants up to 2025.

The commission also urged the state to take advantage of the education component of the World Bank-supported HOPE Education Programme, with up to $500 million earmarked for education.

States were told that to qualify, they must access the 2026 matching grant and implement at least 50 per cent of their 2025 Action Plan.

Responding, Onyeme said updated records showed that Delta had about N1 billion in unutilised funds, contrary to the N8 billion earlier reported.

He added that the state had implemented about 90 per cent of its 2025 Action Plan and had already received its 2026 matching grant.

The UBEC team also highlighted Delta’s technology-driven teacher attendance system, Attend360, as a model that could strengthen accountability in basic education nationwide.

“There is no education or quality learning without a good teacher or without a teacher in the classroom,” the executive secretary noted.

During a visit to the Asagba of Asaba, Prof. Epiphany Azinge, UBEC called for stronger collaboration with traditional institutions.

Azinge described basic education as the foundation of Nigeria’s future and urged UBEC and SUBEBs to ensure no child, including those with disabilities and from disadvantaged backgrounds, is left behind.

UBEC assured the Asagba that it will continue working with states to ensure that investments in basic education yield visible impact in classrooms.

World.title: Industrial Action: Sheathe Your Sword, Exercise Restraint, NCAA Tells Unions
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) has pleaded with aviation unions to sheathe their sword and exercise restraint in the ongoing industrial action which has impacted passengers and other stakeholders.

The authority noted that the matter would have been addressed at the meeting convened by the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development Festus Keyamo last week, but the meeting could not hold as the airline operators failed to honour the invitation.

NCAA, in a statement on Tuesday by its Director General, Capt. Chris Najomo, stated that the appeal became necessary and will be resolved pending the return of the minister, Keyamo, who has been actively working towards resolving the issues.

Najomo assured the travelling public that flight safety remained uncompromised, adding that the authority would continue to exercise its statutory safety oversight responsibilities.

“We appeal to all parties to embrace dialogue and cooperation. We are confident that the matter will be resolved shortly and normal flight operations will resume as soon as practicable.

“The NCAA regrets the inconvenience caused to passengers and appreciates their patience and understanding,” he said.

World.title: Delta Suspends Works Commissioner over Alleged Assault on Gov’s Aide
World.content:
T6Sylvester Idowu in Warri, Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

The Delta State Government yesterday suspended the state Commissioner for Works (Highway and Urban Roads), Hon. Izeze Rume Yakubu Reuben, with immediate effect.

The suspension, according to a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Dr. Kingsley Emu, is to allow security agencies to conduct an impartial investigation into allegations linking the commissioner to the recent assault of the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Protocol, Mr. Simon Mudi, popularly known as ‘Temple’.

The incident reportedly occurred at the Petroleum Training Institute (PTI), Effurun, in Uvwie Local Government Area of the state during the Delta Central meeting of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The SSG said the suspension was necessary to ensure that the investigation was conducted without interference and to establish the facts surrounding the incident.

The state government, he said, remained committed to maintaining public safety, law and order, and the sanctity of human lives under all circumstances.

Dr. Emu stressed that the government’s commitment to these principles remained unwavering, even when individuals or institutions of the state were involved.

“The suspension is expected to remain in force pending the outcome of the investigation by the relevant security agencies,” he said.

World.title: NHRC Demands Immediate Arrest, Prosecution of Sheikh Jingir Over Hate Speech
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has called for the immediate arrest and prosecution of prominent Islamic cleric, Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir, over what it described as hateful and inciting remarks capable of aggravating religious tensions ahead of the 2027 general election.

The Executive Secretary of the commission, Chief Tony Ojukwu, made the demand after the NHRC reviewed a viral video in which the cleric allegedly canvassed religiously exclusive politics and urged his supporters to obtain their permanent voter cards (PVCs) to “show their limit”.

Ojukwu, who condemned the remarks in strong terms, said the cleric’s reference to people of other faiths as “infidels”, coupled with his political exhortations, constituted a dangerous attempt to mobilise citizens along religious lines.

According to him, the statements amounted to hate speech and incitement to religious hatred, with the potential to trigger violence at a time Nigeria is preparing for another politically sensitive electoral cycle.

The NHRC boss said the remarks were inconsistent with the constitutional principles of equality, non-discrimination and peaceful coexistence, as well as Nigeria’s obligations under international human rights instruments.

“The commission finds these remarks to be hate speech and incitement to religious hatred and potential violence. At a time when we are preparing for another general election, such utterances are reckless and dangerous,” he said.

Ojukwu warned that failure by the authorities to respond decisively could encourage other influential religious and political actors to make increasingly provocative statements as the 2027 elections draw closer.

“We cannot afford to look away. If we fail to speak and act now, we embolden both Christian and Muslim clerics and other influential persons to make worse statements in the coming months. That path leads only to crisis,” he said.

Consequently, the commission called on the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant authorities to immediately arrest and prosecute Jingir for alleged hate speech and incitement.

The NHRC insisted that any prosecution should be pursued irrespective of the cleric’s status or political affiliation, arguing that equal application of the law was necessary to deter others from exploiting religious sentiments for political purposes.

The commission’s intervention comes as political actors, religious leaders and civil society groups increasingly turn their attention to the potential impact of identity-based mobilisation on the 2027 electoral process.

Ojukwu further urged religious leaders, traditional rulers and politicians to abandon divisive rhetoric and instead encourage Nigerians to assess political leaders on the basis of competence, service delivery, integrity and respect for fundamental human rights.

He also called on Nigerians to reject identity politics and resist attempts to turn religious affiliation into a tool for political mobilisation.

“The commission will continue to monitor compliance and will engage with security agencies, INEC, and civil society to ensure that the 2027 elections are free from hate and violence,” he said.

The NHRC’s position adds a fresh dimension to the growing debate over the role of religious rhetoric in Nigeria’s electoral politics, particularly as political parties and prospective candidates begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

Jingir has previously been involved in controversies surrounding politically charged religious messaging.

In the run-up to the 2019 general election, he attracted criticism over a video message to followers concerning voting and religious identity.

The latest NHRC intervention therefore places renewed focus on the responsibility of influential religious figures to ensure that political mobilisation does not cross the line into rhetoric capable of threatening peaceful coexistence or electoral stability.

World.title: Journalists Urged to Harness AI to Transform Reporting
World.content:
The future of journalism is being reshaped by Artificial Intelligence (AI), offering unprecedented opportunities to enhance reporting, streamline workflows, and deliver more engaging content to readers worldwide.

The Chief Executive of Chesca Global Solutions Limited, Ms. Franca Ibuzo, stated this in a press statement, noting that “in automated news gathering, AI can scan vast amounts of data, social media feeds, and public records in real time, and help journalists identify breaking stories faster.”

According to her, during fact‑ checking and verification, with misinformation on the rise, AI tools assist in verifying sources, cross‑checking facts, and ensuring accuracy before publication.

She noted that “content personalisation and AI algorithms now tailor news delivery to readers’ interests, improving engagement and ensuring diverse perspectives reach the right audiences.”

Ibuzo added: “Multimedia enhancement, from generating graphics to transcribing interviews, AI reduces repetitive tasks, allowing journalists to focus on news writing.”

“Transcribing and translation are powered by AI, which enables newsrooms to break language barriers, making stories accessible to international audiences instantly.”

She, however, exphasised that “AI is not replacing journalists but rather it is empowering them.

“By leveraging AI responsibly, we can uphold the integrity of journalism while embracing innovation that makes reporting more efficient and impactful.”

“As media organisations adopt AI, ethical considerations remain paramount. Transparency, accountability, and human oversight are essential to ensure that technology strengthens trust rather than undermines it,” she said.

She urged “media organisations management to reiterate their commitment to advancing journalism through innovation by equipping reporters and editors with cutting‑edge tools to deliver credible, timely, and engaging news.”

World.title: NCWS Tasks Women to Vote Wisely, Seeks More Political Positions
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The National Council of Women’s Societies (NCWS) has urged women in Nigeria to mobilise and vote wisely in the 2027 general election in accordance with their conscience.

The President of NCWS, South-West Forum, Mrs. Priscilla Kuye, who made the call in her welcome address at the council’s annual conference held in Ibadan, Oyo State, said women should actively participate in the electoral process and support candidates committed to good governance, the rule of law and promotion of fundamental human rights.

According to her, the council was concerned about insecurity, kidnapping, unemployment, hunger and inadequate access to water and electricity in the country.

“We want good governance and promotion of the rule of law. We want all women and girls to be accorded their fundamental human rights in accordance with our constitution,” she said.

Kuye disclosed that the seminar, which focused on ‘Human Rights, Justice, Action for all Women and Girls in the Society’, was organised to educate women on issues affecting them, particularly ahead of the 2027 elections.

Stating that the conference brought together women from various associations across the South-west geopolitical zone.

In its communiqué, the conference called for the mobilisation and sensitisation of women to vote wisely, while advocating increased representation of women in political positions of responsibility.

The council also urged women to seek more elective and political positions while calling for the empowerment of women through access to low-interest loans to enable them to establish and expand businesses.

The NCWS further encouraged educated women to guide and support less-educated women, while calling on men to stop relegating women to the background in all spheres of life.

It also recommended increased media publicity for the council’s activities, including jingles, interviews, and other platforms to showcase the achievements of its members.

The council proposed the organisation of a mega meeting where political stakeholders and other power brokers would be invited to pledge their support for women.

The communiqué also announced plans to celebrate the centenary birthday of one of the founding mothers of NCWS and its first Secretary-General in 1962, Prof. Adetoun Ogunsheye.

Ogunsheye, according to the council, is Nigeria’s first female professor, and her centenary celebration is scheduled for December 5, 2026.

The NCWS was registered as a society on June 24, 1965, after its formation in Ibadan by women’s organisations seeking to promote women’s education, political participation and economic development.

The organisation has since expanded to all states of Nigeria with a national body.

World.title: RIP | Former Springbok and Bulls hooker dies: Full Test career stats
World.content:
Mark Alexander, the president of SA Rugby, paid tribute to former Springbok hooker "Piston" van Wyk who passed away over the weekend. Image: SA Rugby website

Mark Alexander, the president of SA Rugby, paid tribute to former Springbok hooker Jacobus Frederick Beatrix “Piston” van Wyk, who passed away over the weekend at the age of 82.

Van Wyk, who played for the erstwhile Northern Transvaal and Natal – now the Bulls and Sharks – made 15 Test appearances between 1970 and 1976, starting and ending his Springbok career with Tests against the All Blacks.

Profound sadness

A versatile and aggressive hooker, Van Wyk also toured Australia in 1971 and faced the touring British & Irish Lions in 1974.



“It is with profound sadness that we mourn the passing of Piston van Wyk, a former Springbok whose legacy is etched into the proud history of South African rugby,” said Alexander.

“Piston’s career was marked by his formidable scrummaging strength, his unwavering commitment to the team and his memorable performances against some of the world’s toughest opponents.

“From his debut in the green and gold to his standout contributions in numerous Test victories, Piston embodied the resilience and pride of the Springbok jersey. His presence on the field was a source of inspiration and his dedication to the game reflected the values of discipline, humility and sportsmanship.

“Beyond rugby, Piston carried himself with dignity and integrity, leaving behind a legacy that extends far beyond the scoreboard. His name will forever be remembered among those who helped shape the path for future generations of players.

“We extend our deepest condolences to his family and loved ones. May they find comfort in knowing that his contribution to our sport and our nation will never be forgotten. Piston van Wyk’s memory will live on in the hearts of all who cherish the game of rugby and the values it represents.”

World.title: African players to watch in the 2026/27 Premier League season
World.content:
The 2026/27 Premier League season is almost here, and African football fans will once again have plenty of players to follow when the action gets underway.

The new campaign kicks off on 21 August, with Arsenal hosting newly promoted Coventry City in the opening match.

Here are five African players to watch during the 2026/27 Premier League season.



Amad Diallo – Côte d’Ivoire, Manchester United

Amad Diallo enters the new campaign with something to prove at Manchester United.

The Côte d’Ivoire international remains part of United’s 2026/27 squad and is listed among the club’s forwards.

Amad has already shown flashes of his quality at Old Trafford, including a seven-goal Premier League campaign in 2024/25.



The challenge now is consistency.

With Manchester United looking to compete higher up the Premier League table, Amad could become an increasingly important attacking option if he can stay fit and turn his creativity into regular goals and assists.

African star Mohammed Kudus – Ghana, Tottenham

Mohammed Kudus is one of the most exciting African attackers in the Premier League.



The Ghanaian joined Tottenham from West Ham United and remains part of Spurs’ 2026/27 squad.

His combination of strength, speed and technical ability makes him particularly dangerous when attacking defenders one-on-one.

There is also a tactical reason to watch Kudus this season.



The Premier League’s own analysis of Tottenham’s squad suggested that De Zerbi’s approach could suit Kudus on the right, particularly because of the opportunities created by one-on-one situations in wide areas.

If Tottenham’s new system clicks, Kudus could be one of the biggest beneficiaries.

Omar Marmoush to watch in the Premier League

Omar Marmoush will be one of the most closely watched African players at Manchester City.



The Egyptian forward is part of City’s attacking options and has already demonstrated his ability to score important goals in the Premier League.

His pace and movement give City another way of attacking opponents, particularly when he is allowed to drift into dangerous positions.

Marmoush could also benefit from City’s new era under Enzo Maresca as the club looks to challenge for major honours again.



And there is an intriguing African partnership developing at the Etihad.

Bryan Mbeumo faces another big Premier League test

Bryan Mbeumo will be under considerable pressure to deliver for Manchester United.

The Cameroon international joined United from Brentford in 2025 and remains part of the club’s 2026/27 squad.



Mbeumo has already shown that he can produce goals and assists in the Premier League, and his ability to play across the forward line gives United another attacking option.

He has also demonstrated his ability to perform in big matches.

In February 2026, he scored in Manchester United’s 2-0 victory over Tottenham.



The 2026/27 season could therefore be a defining one for the Cameroonian.

If Mbeumo can combine his goalscoring ability with greater consistency, he could become one of the most influential African players in the league.

Antoine Semenyo takes on a new Premier League challenge

Antoine Semenyo may be the African player with the biggest opportunity to make a statement this season.



The Ghanaian joined Manchester City from Bournemouth in January 2026 after an impressive spell on the south coast.

City signed him on a five-and-a-half-year contract.

Before moving to Manchester, Semenyo had established himself as one of the Premier League’s most dangerous attacking players.



The Premier League noted that he had scored 10 goals and recorded 12 goal contributions before his January move to City.

Now, he has the opportunity to do it on one of the biggest stages in English football.

Semenyo has already given City fans plenty of reasons for optimism during pre-season.



In City’s 3-1 victory over Atletico Madrid in Seoul, he provided two assists for Marmoush, while finishing City’s pre-season tour with four assists in three matches.

The combination of Semenyo and Marmoush could become one of the most exciting African attacking partnerships in the Premier League this season.

World.title: Lisa Koppel cancer battle: Family looked beyond SA for hope
World.content:
Danny K with his late wife, Lisa Koppel, who battled colorectal cancer for nearly three years. Image: @dannykj23

The family of Lisa Koppel has revealed how they searched for hope in South Africa and abroad during her nearly three-year battle with colorectal cancer.

Koppel, the wife of South African singer Danny K, died at the age of 41.

Her family revealed this week that doctors diagnosed her with colorectal cancer in November 2023.



From that moment, Koppel and those closest to her pursued every possible opportunity available to them.

“Together with her family, she searched for hope in South Africa and around the world, pursuing every treatment and every opportunity available to her,” the family said.

“Tragically, despite everything, she could not be saved.”



Family searched for hope

The family did not disclose details about the treatments Koppel received or where she received care abroad.

However, they confirmed that healthcare professionals in South Africa and overseas cared for her during her illness.

“The family is deeply grateful to every doctor, nurse and healthcare professional who cared for Lisa throughout her journey, both in South Africa and abroad.”



Koppel fought the disease away from the public eye.

Her family said she deliberately kept her diagnosis private.

Why Lisa Koppel kept her illness private

Koppel did not want her cancer battle to attract public attention.



“Lisa chose to keep her illness private. She never wanted pity, attention or sympathy,” the family said.

Her children remained at the heart of that decision.

“Above all, she wanted to protect her children and preserve their happiness and innocence for as long as possible.”



The family described Koppel as gentle, humble and brave throughout her illness.

Family reveals reason for speaking out

The family has now revealed Koppel’s diagnosis for one reason: awareness.

Koppel had hoped to eventually use her own experience to raise awareness about colorectal cancer and early detection.



She never got the opportunity.

Her family will now continue that work in her name.

“Lisa hoped that one day she would use her experience to raise awareness of this disease and help others through early detection,” the family said.



The family also urged people with persistent symptoms to speak to a doctor and have them properly investigated.

Family left ‘shattered’

Koppel leaves behind Danny and their three children.

The Koppel and Gundelfinger families said her death had left them “shattered”.



They have asked for prayers, compassion and privacy as they grieve.

The family said Koppel’s illness would not define her.

Instead, they want her remembered for her kindness, humility, courage and devotion to those she loved.
